practice.q: Explain how to read a bar that ends between two numbers on the scale.
practice.ans: Find the two numbers on the scale that the bar is between. If the bar ends halfway, its value is the number halfway between them, such as 25 halfway between 20 and 30.

quiz.q: A bar graph scale counts by 10s. The bar for soccer ends at the 6th line above 0. What number does it show?
A bar graph shows votes: red 12, blue 20 and green 8. Which statement is true?
ch: Blue got 8 more votes than red
Blue got 28 more votes than green

quiz.q: A bar graph shows cans collected: week 1, 45 cans; week 2, 30 cans; week 3, 55 cans. How many cans were collected in all?
A bar graph shows favorite instruments: drums 14, guitar 9, piano 11 and violin 6. How many more students chose drums or piano than guitar or violin?
A bar graph scale counts by 4s. A bar ends halfway between 12 and 16. What does the bar show?
A bar graph shows that 4 classes collected 30, 25, 40 and 35 books. The goal for each class was 30 books. How many classes met or beat the goal?
Kofi drew a bar graph with the scale 0, 5, 10, 20, 40. Explain what is wrong with his scale.
quiz.ans: The spaces on a scale must stand for equal amounts. His scale jumps by 5, then 10, then 20, so the bars would not compare fairly. He should count by the same number each time, such as 5s.

lessons.name: Measuring to the nearest half and quarter inch

practice.q: A crayon ends halfway between the 3-inch and 4-inch marks on a ruler. How long is it?
practice.h: Look at the mark halfway between 3 and 4.

practice.q: On a ruler, how many quarter-inch spaces are between 0 and 1 inch?
practice.h: A quarter is one of four equal parts.

practice.q: A leaf measures 2 1/4 inches. How many quarter inches long is it?
practice.h: Each inch has 4 quarter inches. Count the quarters in 2 inches, then add 1 more.

practice.q: A ruler is marked in quarter inches. A pencil ends at the first mark after the 5-inch mark. How long is the pencil?
practice.h: Each small space is 1/4 inch.

practice.q: A ribbon starts at 0 and ends at the 2 1/2-inch mark on a ruler. How many inches long is the ribbon?
practice.h: When an object starts at 0, its length is the number where it ends.

practice.q: Kim lined up one end of a stick at the 1-inch mark on a ruler. The other end was at the 4-inch mark. She says the stick is 4 inches long. Explain her mistake.
practice.ans: She did not start at 0. The stick goes from 1 to 4, which is 3 inches.

quiz.q: Which mark on a ruler is halfway between 6 and 7 inches?
A worm is 3 3/4 inches long. Another worm is 1/4 inch longer. How long is the second worm, in inches?
Which length is the longest?
A snail crawls from the 2-inch mark to the 5 1/2-inch mark on a ruler. How many inches did it crawl?
Which length is closest to 2 inches?
A pencil measures 5 2/4 inches. Which is another way to write its length?
Explain why measuring to the nearest quarter inch can be more exact than measuring to the nearest inch.
quiz.ans: Quarter inches are smaller units. Measuring with smaller units lets you get closer to the real length instead of rounding to a whole inch.

lessons.name: Line plots of measurement data

practice.q: A line plot shows the lengths of 10 shells. There are 3 Xs above 1 1/2 inches. How many shells are 1 1/2 inches long?
practice.h: Each X stands for one shell.

practice.q: A line plot of pencil lengths has 2 Xs at 4 inches, 1 X at 4 1/4 inches, 4 Xs at 4 1/2 inches and 3 Xs at 4 3/4 inches. Which length is most common?
practice.h: Which length has the most Xs above it?

practice.q: A line plot shows pencil lengths: 2 Xs at 4 inches, 1 X at 4 1/4 inches, 4 Xs at 4 1/2 inches and 3 Xs at 4 3/4 inches. How many pencils were measured?
practice.h: Count every X.

practice.q: Which number line is best for a line plot of lengths measured to the nearest quarter inch?
ch: one marked in whole inches only
practice.h: The marks should match the units used to measure.

practice.q: A line plot of plant heights shows 2 Xs at 3 inches, 5 Xs at 3 1/2 inches and 1 X at 4 inches. How many plants are taller than 3 inches?
practice.h: Which heights are greater than 3 inches? Add their Xs.

practice.q: Explain how to make a line plot of these ribbon lengths: 2 1/2, 3, 2 1/2, 3 1/2 and 3 inches.
practice.ans: Draw a number line from 2 to 4 inches marked in halves. Put one X above the line for each ribbon: 2 Xs above 2 1/2, 2 Xs above 3 and 1 X above 3 1/2.

quiz.q: A line plot shows 4 Xs above 5 inches. How many objects measured 5 inches?
A line plot shows 2 leaves at 1 1/4 inches, 3 at 1 1/2 inches, 6 at 1 3/4 inches and 1 at 2 inches. How many leaves are longer than 1 1/2 inches?
A line plot shows 2 leaves at 1 1/4 inches, 3 at 1 1/2 inches, 6 at 1 3/4 inches and 1 at 2 inches. How many more leaves are 1 3/4 inches long than 1 1/4 inches long?
A line plot shows the lengths of 8 crayons. Which statement could NOT be true?
Which set of measurements needs a line plot marked in quarter inches?
A line plot shows the lengths of 12 worms: 3 at 2 inches, 4 at 2 1/4 inches, 3 at 2 1/2 inches and 2 at 2 3/4 inches. How many worms are shorter than 2 1/2 inches?
Students measured 6 sticks: 3 1/2, 4, 3 1/2, 4 1/2, 3 1/2 and 4 inches. Which describes the correct line plot?
ch: 3 Xs at 3 1/2, 2 Xs at 4, 1 X at 4 1/2
2 Xs at 3 1/2, 3 Xs at 4, 1 X at 4 1/2
3 Xs at 3 1/2, 1 X at 4, 2 Xs at 4 1/2

quiz.q: Leo made a line plot of pencil lengths. He spaced 4, 4 1/4 and 4 1/2 far apart but put 4 3/4 and 5 close together. Explain why this is a problem.
quiz.ans: On a number line, equal jumps must have equal spaces. If the spaces are uneven, the line plot gives a wrong picture of how the lengths compare.

test.q: In a picture graph, each smiley face stands for 5 students. A row has 7 smiley faces. How many students does the row show?
A ribbon ends halfway between the 5-inch and 6-inch marks on a ruler. How long is the ribbon?
A bar graph scale counts 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. A bar ends at the 30 line. What number does it show?
In a picture graph, each ball stands for 4 students. Soccer has 6 balls and basketball has 3 balls. How many more students chose soccer than basketball?
In a picture graph, each symbol stands for 2 books. A row has 7 and a half symbols. How many books does the row show?
Which key would make a picture graph of 40, 25 and 35 easiest to draw?
A bar graph shows laps run: Rey 12, Ada 16, Sam 9 and Lu 15. Which statement is true?
ch: Ada ran 7 more laps than Sam
Rey and Lu ran the same number of laps
Lu ran 4 fewer laps than Rey

test.q: Rey ran 12 laps, Ada ran 16, Sam ran 9 and Lu ran 15. How many laps did they run in all?
A bar graph of canned food shows Room 1 collected 35 cans, Room 2 collected 50 and Room 3 collected 25. The goal was 150 cans. How many more cans are needed to reach the goal?
A picture graph shows trees planted. Each tree symbol stands for 10 trees. Park A has 4 symbols, Park B has 2 and a half symbols and Park C has 6 symbols. How many trees were planted in all?
A bar graph scale counts by 10s. A bar ends halfway between 30 and 40. What does the bar show?
A bean sprout is 3 1/4 inches tall. On a ruler marked in quarter inches, where does the sprout end?
Which length is between 2 1/4 inches and 2 3/4 inches?
A line plot of crayon lengths shows 4 Xs at 3 inches, 2 Xs at 3 1/4 inches and 5 Xs at 3 1/2 inches. How many crayons were measured?

A line plot of feather lengths shows 1 X at 4 inches, 3 Xs at 4 1/4 inches, 6 Xs at 4 1/2 inches and 2 Xs at 5 inches. How many more feathers are 4 1/2 inches long than are 4 1/4 inches or 5 inches long?
A line plot shows hand spans. The most Xs are above 5 1/2 inches, and there are no Xs above 6 1/4 inches. Which statement must be true?
ch: The most common hand span is 5 1/2 inches
The longest hand span is 5 1/2 inches

test.q: A survey asked 30 students to pick one fruit. Apples got 12 votes, bananas got 8 and the rest chose grapes. Which statement is true?
ch: Grapes got 10 votes, 2 more than bananas

test.q: Which question can be answered with a line plot of measurement data?
ch: How many plants are 4 1/2 inches tall?
What is the class's favorite color?
On which day did it rain?

test.q: A picture graph uses a key where each car symbol stands for 10 cars. Explain how you would show 45 cars.
test.ans: Draw 4 whole symbols for 40 cars and half of a symbol for 5 more cars, because half of 10 is 5.

test.q: Rina measured a leaf as 3 inches. Mo measured the same leaf as 3 1/4 inches. Explain how both could be measuring correctly.
test.ans: Rina measured to the nearest inch and Mo measured to the nearest quarter inch. 3 1/4 is closer to 3 than to 4, so to the nearest inch it is 3 inches. Mo's measurement is more exact.

test.q: Jo read a bar graph whose scale counts by 5s. A bar ends at the third line above 0, and Jo said the bar shows 3. Explain the mistake and give the correct value.
test.ans: Jo counted the lines instead of reading the scale. Each line stands for 5 more, so the third line above 0 is 15.

test.q: Students measured the heights of 10 bean plants to the nearest quarter inch: 2 1/4, 2 1/2, 2 1/2, 3, 2 3/4, 2 1/2, 3, 2 1/4, 2 1/2 and 2 3/4 inches. (a) Make a line plot of the data. (b) Which height is most common? (c) How many plants are taller than 2 1/2 inches? (d) Write one more question that can be answered with your line plot, and answer it.
rub: Accurate line plot marked in quarter inches (2 Xs at 2 1/4, 4 at 2 1/2, 2 at 2 3/4, 2 at 3); most common 2 1/2 inches; 4 plants taller than 2 1/2 inches; a sensible new question answered correctly.
Line plot and answers mostly correct with one small error.
Line plot partly correct, or answers do not match the plot.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 7: Geometry and measurement word problems
units.el: Provide labeled shape cards, geoboards and string for measuring around shapes. Pre-teach "perimeter", "quadrilateral", "parallel", "right angle" and "attribute", and have students trace the outside of a shape while saying "perimeter".

lessons.name: Two-step word problems with all four operations

practice.q: A packet has 6 stickers. Ana buys 7 packets and gives 9 stickers to her brother. How many stickers does she have left?
practice.h: First find how many stickers are in 7 packets.

practice.q: 48 students go on a trip in 6 vans, with the same number of students in each van. Each van also has 1 adult driver. How many people ride in each van?
practice.h: Find the number of students in each van first, then add the driver.

practice.q: Leo had 50 cents. He bought 4 pencils for 8 cents each. Which equation finds m, the cents he has left?
practice.h: First find the cost of the pencils. Then take that away from 50.

practice.q: A farmer has 72 eggs. He packs them in cartons of 6, then sells 5 cartons. How many full cartons are left?
practice.h: First find how many cartons he fills.

practice.q: Which is the best estimate for 289 + 412 - 198, rounding each number to the nearest hundred?
practice.h: Round each number to the nearest hundred first.

practice.q: Write a two-step word problem for 5 x 6 + 8 and solve it.
practice.ans: A class has 5 tables with 6 students at each table, and 8 more students join. How many students are there? 5 x 6 = 30 and 30 + 8 = 38 students.

quiz.q: Luis buys 3 shirts that cost $9 each. He pays with a $50 bill. How many dollars of change does he get?
56 crayons are shared equally by 8 students. Then each student gets 4 more crayons. How many crayons does each student have now?
A library has 4 shelves with 9 books each and 3 shelves with 8 books each. How many books are on the shelves?
Mia had some beads. She used 18 beads, then bought 25 more. Now she has 60 beads. Which equation finds b, the number of beads she started with?
Cheng runs 4 laps each day for 7 days. His goal is 40 laps. How many more laps must he run?
A pack has 8 markers. A class buys 5 packs and loses 6 markers. Raj says 34 markers are left. Which check shows his answer is reasonable?
ch: 5 x 8 = 40, and 40 take away about 6 is about 34

quiz.q: Kim solved "There are 7 rows of 6 chairs, and 9 chairs are taken away. How many are left?" by writing 7 + 6 - 9 = 4. Explain her mistake and solve the problem.
quiz.ans: She added 7 and 6 instead of multiplying. There are 7 groups of 6, so 7 x 6 = 42 chairs, and 42 - 9 = 33 chairs are left.

lessons.name: Attributes of two-dimensional shapes

practice.q: Which shape is a quadrilateral?
ch: a closed shape with 4 straight sides
a closed shape with 3 straight sides
a closed shape with 5 straight sides
practice.h: "Quad" means four.

practice.q: Which shape always has 4 right angles and 4 sides of equal length?
practice.h: Think about which shape has both of these attributes every time.

practice.q: Which statement is always true?
practice.h: A rectangle needs 4 right angles. Does a square have them?

practice.q: A shape has 4 sides. Two of its sides are parallel and the other two sides are not parallel. What shape is it?
practice.h: In rectangles, squares and rhombuses, both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

practice.q: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
practice.h: Look at each corner of a rectangle.

practice.q: Explain why a rhombus might not be a square.
practice.ans: A rhombus has 4 equal sides, but its angles do not have to be right angles. A square must have 4 right angles, so a rhombus with slanted corners is not a square.

quiz.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
Which shape has exactly 3 sides?
Which shape is a quadrilateral but NOT a rectangle?
ch: a rhombus with no right angles
a shape with 4 sides and 4 right angles

quiz.q: A shape has 4 right angles. Two sides are 6 cm long and two sides are 3 cm long. What is the shape?
Which statement is true?
ch: A square is a rhombus, a rectangle and a quadrilateral
A rectangle is always a rhombus
A trapezoid always has 4 right angles

quiz.q: Lily draws 3 quadrilaterals and 2 pentagons. How many sides does she draw in all?
Sam says a shape with 4 straight sides that are all different lengths is not a quadrilateral. Explain whether he is right.
quiz.ans: He is not right. A quadrilateral is any closed shape with 4 straight sides. The sides do not have to be the same length.

lessons.name: Solving problems with perimeter

practice.q: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
practice.h: Add all four sides: 7 + 4 + 7 + 4.

practice.q: A triangle has sides of 5 inches, 6 inches and 8 inches. What is its perimeter in inches?
practice.h: Perimeter is the total length of all the sides.

practice.q: A square garden has a perimeter of 32 feet. How many feet long is each side?
practice.h: A square has 4 equal sides. What number times 4 is 32?

practice.q: Which situation is about perimeter?
ch: putting a fence around a yard
practice.h: Perimeter is the distance around a shape.

practice.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 meters. Its length is 9 meters. What is its width in meters?
practice.h: The two lengths use 18 meters. What is left for the two widths?

practice.q: Explain why you can find the perimeter of an 8 by 3 rectangle by doubling 8 + 3.
practice.ans: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths. 8 + 3 is one length and one width, so doubling it gives all four sides: 11 + 11 = 22 units.

quiz.q: A square tile has sides of 9 cm. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
A pentagon has 5 sides that are each 7 inches long. What is its perimeter in inches?
A picture frame is 12 inches long and 9 inches wide. How many inches of ribbon fit exactly around the frame?
Ms. Ali puts a border around a bulletin board that is 6 feet by 4 feet. The border comes in rolls of 5 feet. How many rolls does she need?
A quadrilateral has a perimeter of 26 cm. Three of its sides are 5 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm. How long is the fourth side?
Which rectangle has a perimeter of 16 units?
Rafa found the perimeter of a 6 by 2 rectangle by multiplying 6 x 2 = 12. Explain his mistake and find the perimeter.
quiz.ans: He found the area, not the perimeter. Perimeter is the distance around: 6 + 2 + 6 + 2 = 16 units.

lessons.name: Problem solving with perimeter and area

practice.q: Which two rectangles have the same perimeter but different areas?
practice.h: Find the perimeter and the area of each rectangle.

practice.q: Of all the rectangles with whole-number sides and an area of 12 square units, what is the greatest perimeter?
practice.h: List all the rectangles with an area of 12: 1 by 12, 2 by 6 and 3 by 4.

practice.q: Ty has 20 feet of fence for a rectangular pen. He makes it 6 feet long. What is the area of the pen in square feet?
practice.h: First use the perimeter to find the width.

practice.q: One garden is 4 meters by 4 meters. Another is 2 meters by 6 meters. Which statement is true?
ch: They have the same perimeter, but the square has more area
They have the same area and the same perimeter
The 2 by 6 garden has more area
practice.h: Find the perimeter and area of each garden.

practice.q: A rectangular patio has a perimeter of 24 meters. Its width is 4 meters. What is its area in square meters?
practice.h: Find the length first. The two widths use 8 meters.

practice.q: Two rectangles each have an area of 16 square units. Explain how they can have different perimeters.
practice.ans: A 2 by 8 rectangle has a perimeter of 20 units, and a 4 by 4 square has a perimeter of 16 units. Area counts the squares inside, but the perimeter depends on how the squares are arranged; a long, thin shape has more outside edge.

quiz.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 18 inches and a length of 5 inches. What is its area in square inches?
Which rectangle has an area of 24 square units and a perimeter of 20 units?
A square has an area of 25 square feet. What is its perimeter in feet?
Nora is building a rectangular pen with 16 meters of fence. She wants the greatest area possible with whole-number side lengths. What is that area in square meters?
A rectangle is 2 by 10. Kai makes a new rectangle with the same perimeter that is 5 units wide. How does its area compare with the first rectangle's?
ch: It is 35 square units, which is 15 more
It is 20 square units, the same
It is 50 square units, which is 30 more
It is 24 square units, which is 4 more

quiz.q: A room is 7 meters by 6 meters. Baseboard goes all the way around the room except for a doorway 1 meter wide. How many meters of baseboard are needed?
Bea says that if two rectangles have the same area, they must have the same perimeter. Give an example that shows she is wrong.
quiz.ans: A 1 by 6 rectangle and a 2 by 3 rectangle both have an area of 6 square units, but their perimeters are 14 units and 10 units.

test.q: A rectangle is 8 meters by 5 meters. What is its perimeter in meters?
Which shape has exactly 5 sides?
Which quadrilateral is always both a rectangle and a rhombus?
A square has sides of 6 inches. What is its perimeter in inches?
A hexagon has 6 sides that are each 5 cm long. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
A square playground has a perimeter of 36 meters. How many meters long is each side?
Which statement about quadrilaterals is always true?
A quadrilateral has four sides that are each 6 cm long, but it has no right angles. What is it?
Which rectangle has the same perimeter as a 6 by 2 rectangle?
Which situation asks for area?
ch: how much carpet covers a floor
how much fence goes around a field
how much ribbon goes around a box lid
how far it is around a running track

test.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 22 inches and a width of 4 inches. What is its length in inches?
Pedro buys 4 notebooks for $3 each and 2 pens for $5 each. He pays with a $30 bill. How many dollars of change does he get?
63 students are split equally into 7 teams. Each team then splits into groups of 3. How many groups does each team make?
A garden is 9 feet long and 4 feet wide. Fencing costs $2 per foot. How many dollars does it cost to fence all the way around the garden?
A rectangular playground has a perimeter of 30 meters and a length of 10 meters. What is its area in square meters?
Two rectangles each have a perimeter of 20 cm. One is 9 cm by 1 cm and the other is 5 cm by 5 cm. Which statement is true?
ch: The 5 by 5 square has 16 more square centimeters of area
The 9 by 1 rectangle has more area
The 5 by 5 square has 5 more square centimeters of area

test.q: Lia makes a rectangle using all 24 of her square tiles. Which rectangle has the smallest perimeter?
Which is the best estimate for 612 - 289 + 98, rounding each number to the nearest hundred?
Explain how a square and a rhombus are alike and how they are different.
test.ans: Both are quadrilaterals with 4 equal sides. A square always has 4 right angles, but a rhombus does not have to.

test.q: Nate says the perimeter of a 7 by 3 rectangle is 10 because 7 + 3 = 10. Explain his mistake.
test.ans: He added only two sides. A rectangle has 4 sides, so the perimeter is 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 units.

test.q: Describe two rectangles that have the same perimeter but different areas. Give the perimeter and area of each.
test.ans: For example, a 2 by 6 rectangle has a perimeter of 16 units and an area of 12 square units, and a 4 by 4 square has a perimeter of 16 units and an area of 16 square units.

test.q: The class has exactly 24 meters of fence to build a rectangular garden with whole-number side lengths. (a) List at least three different rectangles that use all 24 meters. (b) Find the area of each one. (c) Which rectangle gives the most space to plant? Explain. (d) One seed packet covers 4 square meters. How many packets are needed for the rectangle with the most space?
rub: At least three correct rectangles (from 1 by 11, 2 by 10, 3 by 9, 4 by 8, 5 by 7, 6 by 6) with correct areas (11, 20, 27, 32, 35, 36); 6 by 6 gives the most space (36 square meters); 36 / 4 = 9 packets; clear explanations.
Correct rectangles and areas with one small error or an incomplete explanation.
Some correct rectangles, or confuses area and perimeter in one part.
Little correct work.

math|4.about: Fourth grade extends place value to 1,000,000 and the standard algorithms for addition and subtraction, solves metric measurement problems, multiplies and divides multi-digit numbers, measures and classifies angles and figures, builds fraction equivalence and operations with like denominators, connects fractions to decimals, and solves customary measurement problems.
std: Solve multistep word problems with whole numbers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted.
Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using place value strategies.
Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors.
Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, and solve word problems with them.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number.
Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

units.name: Module 1: Place value, rounding and algorithms for addition and subtraction
units.el: Use a place value chart to the millions with labeled periods. Pre-teach "period", "expanded form", "estimate", "regroup" and "difference", read multi-step problems twice and sketch a tape diagram together.

lessons.name: Place value and the times-ten relationship

practice.q: In 47,382, what is the value of the 7?
practice.h: Name the place of the 7 first.

practice.q: How many times as great is the value of the 3 in 300 as the value of the 3 in 30?
practice.h: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.
Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left.

practice.q: Which number is the same as 36 hundreds?
practice.h: 10 hundreds make 1 thousand. How many thousands and hundreds are in 36 hundreds?
Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right.

practice.q: Explain why the 5 in 5,000 has 10 times the value of the 5 in 500.
practice.ans: 5,000 is 5 thousands and 500 is 5 hundreds. One thousand is 10 hundreds, so 5 thousands is 10 times as much as 5 hundreds.

quiz.q: What is the value of the 6 in 862,415?
In which number is the 4 worth 10 times as much as the 4 in 7,430?
A town library has 4,500 books. The city library has 10 times as many books. How many books does the city library have?
How many thousands are in 230,000?
Malik says the 2 in 52,000 and the 2 in 25,000 have the same value. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: The 2 in 52,000 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 2,000. The 2 in 25,000 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 20,000, which is 10 times as much.

lessons.name: Reading, writing and comparing multi-digit numbers

practice.q: Which shows 30,000 + 4,000 + 50 + 6 in standard form?
practice.h: Write a 0 in any place that has no value.

practice.q: Which is the word form of 205,318?
ch: two hundred five thousand, three hundred eighteen
two hundred fifty thousand, three hundred eighteen
two hundred five thousand, thirty-one hundred eight
practice.h: Read the period before the comma, say "thousand", then read the rest.

practice.q: Which symbol makes 68,904 __ 69,804 true?
practice.h: Compare the digits from the greatest place to the least.

practice.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
practice.h: Compare the thousands digits first, then the hundreds digits.

practice.q: What number is 1,000 more than 499,500?
practice.h: Add 1 to the thousands place and watch for regrouping.

practice.q: Write 407,060 in expanded form and explain why there are zeros in the number.
practice.ans: 400,000 + 7,000 + 60. The zeros show there are no ten thousands, no hundreds and no ones.

quiz.q: Which is 600,000 + 20,000 + 900 + 4 in standard form?
Which number is greatest?
What number is 10,000 less than 93,450?
Town A has 87,420 people and Town B has 87,240 people. Which statement is true?
What number is 100 more than 39,950?
Which digit makes 5_2,817 > 563,000 true?
Tia says 9,999 > 10,000 because 9 is greater than 1. Explain her mistake.
quiz.ans: She compared the first digits without looking at their places. 10,000 has a digit in the ten thousands place and 9,999 does not, so 10,000 is greater.

lessons.name: Rounding multi-digit whole numbers

practice.q: Round 34,682 to the nearest thousand.
practice.h: Is 34,682 closer to 34,000 or to 35,000?

practice.q: Round 451,276 to the nearest ten thousand.
practice.h: Which two ten thousands is it between? Look at the thousands digit.

practice.q: Round 7,950 to the nearest hundred.
practice.h: 7,950 is between 7,900 and 8,000. Where is the halfway point?

practice.q: Which number rounds to 60,000 when rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
practice.h: Numbers from 55,000 up to 64,999 round to 60,000.

practice.q: A stadium had 38,477 fans. A reporter rounded the number to the nearest thousand. What number did she report?
practice.h: Look at the hundreds digit.

practice.q: Explain how a vertical number line helps you round 2,350 to the nearest thousand.
practice.ans: Put 2,000 at the bottom, 3,000 at the top and 2,500 at the halfway point. 2,350 is below the halfway point, so it rounds to 2,000.

quiz.q: Round 6,481 to the nearest hundred.
Round 283,519 to the nearest hundred thousand.
Round 999,500 to the nearest thousand.
Which is the estimate of 48,302 + 21,815 when each number is rounded to the nearest thousand?
A whole number rounded to the nearest thousand is 9,000. What is the greatest the number could be?
Estimate 3,642 + 2,489 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred. What is the estimate?
Lucy rounded 46,519 to the nearest ten thousand and got 47,000. Explain her mistake and give the correct answer.
quiz.ans: She rounded to the nearest thousand instead of the nearest ten thousand. 46,519 is between 40,000 and 50,000 and is past the halfway point of 45,000, so it rounds to 50,000.

lessons.name: Adding and subtracting with the standard algorithms

practice.h: Line up the places. Regroup when a place has 10 or more.
Rename 1 ten thousand as 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones.
Watch for regrouping in every place.
Check each place before you subtract. Do you need to rename?

practice.q: Which equation is a good way to check 9,023 - 4,567 = 4,456?
practice.h: Addition undoes subtraction.

practice.q: Explain each regrouping step when you add 2,768 + 1,457.
practice.ans: Ones: 8 + 7 = 15, write 5 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 6 + 5 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 7 + 4 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 thousand. Thousands: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. The sum is 4,225.

quiz.q: Which sum is closest to 80,000?
What is the missing digit? 4_,382 + 25,000 = 71,382
Dana subtracted 5,002 - 1,876 and got 4,874. Explain her mistake and find the correct answer.
quiz.ans: In each place she subtracted the smaller digit from the larger digit instead of renaming. She needed to rename a thousand as hundreds, tens and ones. 5,002 - 1,876 = 3,126.

lessons.name: Multi-step addition and subtraction word problems

practice.q: A store had 12,450 water bottles. It sold 3,875 on Saturday and 4,290 on Sunday. How many bottles are left?
practice.h: Find the total sold first, or subtract one day at a time.

practice.q: Farm A grew 24,600 pounds of oranges. Farm B grew 5,850 pounds more than Farm A. How many pounds did the two farms grow in all?
practice.h: First find Farm B's amount, then add the two farms.

practice.q: Kaya wants a bike that costs $1,250. She has saved $486 and gets $350 for her birthday. Which expression shows how much more money she needs?
practice.h: Find how much she has in all, then compare it with the cost.

practice.q: A school library had 8,325 books. It gave away 1,460 old books and bought 2,075 new books. How many books does it have now?
practice.h: Subtract the books given away, then add the new books.

practice.q: A city recycled 38,912 cans in May and 41,276 cans in June. About how many cans is that in all, rounding each number to the nearest thousand?
practice.h: Round each number to the nearest thousand, then add.

practice.q: Explain how a tape diagram helps you solve this problem: A park had 9,200 visitors on Saturday, which was 2,750 more than on Sunday. How many visitors came on Sunday?
practice.ans: Saturday's bar is longer than Sunday's bar by 2,750. Removing that extra part leaves Sunday's bar: 9,200 - 2,750 = 6,450 visitors.

quiz.q: A truck can carry 15,000 pounds. It is loaded with 6,875 pounds of rice and 4,950 pounds of beans. How many more pounds can it carry?

A train carried 2,345 passengers. A second train carried 1,208 more passengers than the first. A third train carried 975 fewer passengers than the second. How many passengers did the 3 trains carry in all?
A plane is flying at 28,750 feet. It climbs 6,400 feet, then drops 3,150 feet. At what height is it flying now, in feet?
A family drives 1,284 miles to visit relatives and the same distance back home. They have driven 1,950 miles so far. How many miles are left?
A bakery made 3,600 rolls. It sold 2,145 rolls in the morning and 876 rolls in the afternoon. How many rolls were not sold?
Ben solved a problem and got 12,560, but his estimate was about 9,000. What should he do?
ch: Check his work, because the answer is far from the estimate
Keep the answer, because estimates are never close

quiz.q: Rosa solved this problem: "A theater sold 4,580 tickets on Friday and 3,920 tickets on Saturday. How many more tickets were sold on Friday?" She added and got 8,500. Explain her mistake and find the answer.
quiz.ans: "How many more" asks for the difference between the two days, so she should subtract: 4,580 - 3,920 = 660 more tickets.

test.q: What is the value of the 8 in 386,214?
Round 72,649 to the nearest thousand.
Which is 200,000 + 7,000 + 30 + 9 in standard form?
Which comparison is true?
Which number rounds to 400,000 when rounded to the nearest hundred thousand?
How many tens are in 4,500?
Which list is in order from greatest to least?
A website had 245,860 visits in March and 187,945 visits in April. How many more visits were there in March?
What number is 100,000 more than 912,500?
A county planted 14,250 trees one year and 9,875 trees the next year. The goal is 30,000 trees. How many more trees must be planted to reach the goal?
A zoo had 6,412 visitors on Friday. Saturday had 2,389 more visitors than Friday. Sunday had 1,045 fewer visitors than Saturday. How many visitors came on Sunday?
Mr. Ruiz's car showed 38,560 miles before a road trip and 41,215 miles after it. How many miles long was the trip?
Which estimate of 61,827 - 29,370 uses rounding to the nearest thousand?
The digit 5 appears twice in 552,148. How does the value of the first 5 compare with the value of the second 5?
A number rounded to the nearest ten thousand is 80,000. Which could the number be?
Use place value to explain why 10 x 2,500 = 25,000.
test.ans: Multiplying by 10 makes each digit worth 10 times as much, so each digit moves one place to the left. 2 thousands become 2 ten thousands and 5 hundreds become 5 thousands, which is 25,000.

test.q: Jae added 38,476 + 5,219 by lining up the numbers on the left and got 90,666. Explain his mistake and find the correct sum.
test.ans: He lined up the digits by their left edges instead of by place value, so he added thousands to ten thousands. Lining up ones with ones gives 38,476 + 5,219 = 43,695.

test.q: Write a two-step word problem that can be solved with 12,000 - (4,350 + 2,875). Solve it.
test.ans: A school has $12,000 for supplies. It spends $4,350 on books and $2,875 on computers. How much is left? 4,350 + 2,875 = 7,225 and 12,000 - 7,225 = $4,775.

test.q: Three schools are collecting cans for a food bank. Lincoln collected 12,486 cans, Valley collected 9,758 cans and Oak collected 14,075 cans. Their goal is 40,000 cans in all. (a) Estimate the total by rounding each number to the nearest thousand. (b) Find the exact total. (c) How many more cans do they need to reach the goal? (d) If Valley collects 3,500 more cans, which school will have collected the most? Show your work and use your estimate to check that your answers are reasonable.
rub: (a) 12,000 + 10,000 + 14,000 = 36,000; (b) 36,319; (c) 3,681; (d) Valley would have 13,258, so Oak (14,075) still has the most; clear work and a reasonableness check.
All parts correct with gaps in the work or check, or one small error with clear work.
Two parts correct, or a workable strategy with regrouping errors.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 2: Unit conversions and problem solving with metric measurement
units.el: Keep a two-column conversion chart (km and m, m and cm, kg and g, L and mL) on each desk and show a real meter stick, liter bottle and 1-kilogram bag. Pre-teach "convert", "kilo-", "centi-" and "milli-".

lessons.name: Converting metric units of length

practice.q: How many meters are in 1 kilometer?
practice.h: "Kilo" means one thousand.

practice.q: How many meters are in 4 kilometers?
practice.h: Each kilometer is 1,000 meters.

practice.q: How many centimeters are in 6 meters?
practice.h: 1 meter is 100 centimeters.

practice.q: Which is equal to 2 km 350 m?
practice.h: Change the kilometers to meters first, then add the meters.

practice.q: A trail is 5 km 80 m long. How many meters long is the trail?
practice.h: 80 meters is less than 100 meters. Which places will be zero?

practice.q: Explain why the number of centimeters is greater than the number of meters when you measure the same length.
practice.ans: A centimeter is a much smaller unit than a meter; 100 centimeters fit in 1 meter. It takes more of a smaller unit to cover the same length, so the number is greater.

quiz.q: How many meters are in 7 kilometers?
How many centimeters are in 3 meters 45 centimeters?
Which length is the longest?
A race is 10 kilometers long. Lia has run 6,500 meters. How many more meters does she have to run?
Which is equal to 4,060 meters?
A ribbon is 2 meters long. Maya cuts off 3 pieces that are each 45 centimeters long. How many centimeters of ribbon are left?
Omar says 5 km 30 m = 530 m. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: 5 km is 5,000 meters, not 500 meters. 5,000 + 30 = 5,030 meters.

lessons.name: Converting metric units of mass and liquid volume

practice.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
practice.h: "Kilo" means one thousand.

practice.q: Which unit would you use to measure the medicine in a spoon?
practice.h: A spoon holds a very small amount of liquid.

practice.q: How many grams are in 6 kilograms 250 grams?
practice.h: Change the kilograms to grams, then add.

practice.q: How many milliliters are in 3 liters?
practice.h: 1 liter is 1,000 milliliters.

practice.q: Which is equal to 7,008 grams?
practice.h: How many whole kilograms are in 7,008 grams? How many grams are left?

practice.q: Make a conversion table for 1, 2, 3 and 4 liters in milliliters, and describe the pattern.
practice.ans: 1 L = 1,000 mL, 2 L = 2,000 mL, 3 L = 3,000 mL and 4 L = 4,000 mL. Each time the liters go up by 1, the milliliters go up by 1,000.

quiz.q: How many milliliters are in 5 liters?
Which mass is the greatest?
A bag of flour has a mass of 2 kilograms. A baker uses 750 grams. How many grams are left?
A water jug holds 4 liters 200 milliliters. How many milliliters does it hold?
A recipe needs 1 L 500 mL of broth. Which amount is equal?
Tomas pours 250 milliliters of juice into each of 6 cups from a 2-liter bottle. How many milliliters are left in the bottle?
Ava says 2 kg is less than 1,500 g because 2 is less than 1,500. Explain her mistake.
quiz.ans: She compared numbers that use different units. 2 kg = 2,000 g, which is more than 1,500 g.

lessons.name: Adding and subtracting mixed metric units

practice.q: 3 m 45 cm + 2 m 70 cm = ?
practice.h: Add the centimeters. If you have 100 or more, make a new meter.

practice.q: What is 5 kg 300 g - 2 kg 650 g, in grams?
practice.h: You can convert both masses to grams, then subtract.
There are not enough milliliters to subtract 500. Rename 1 liter as 1,000 mL.

practice.q: What is 7 km 600 m + 3 km 800 m, in meters?
practice.h: Convert each length to meters, or add the meters and make a new kilometer.

practice.q: A box has a mass of 1 kg 400 g. A second box is 850 g heavier. What is the mass of the second box in grams?
practice.h: Change 1 kg 400 g to grams first.

practice.q: Explain two ways to solve 6 m 20 cm - 3 m 85 cm.
practice.ans: Convert to centimeters: 620 cm - 385 cm = 235 cm, which is 2 m 35 cm. Or rename 1 meter as 100 cm: 5 m 120 cm - 3 m 85 cm = 2 m 35 cm.

quiz.q: What is 9 L 100 mL - 4 L 350 mL, in milliliters?
What is 12 km 50 m - 7 km 900 m, in meters?
Which equals 8 m 5 cm - 2 m 40 cm?
Lena's backpack has a mass of 3 kg 250 g. She adds a book with a mass of 875 g and a water bottle with a mass of 600 g. What is the new mass in grams?
Which sum is exactly 5 L?
Kai added 4 m 65 cm + 1 m 50 cm and wrote 5 m 115 cm. Is his answer correct? Explain a better way to write it.
quiz.ans: The amount is correct, but 115 cm is more than 1 meter. 115 cm = 1 m 15 cm, so the sum is better written as 6 m 15 cm.

lessons.name: Metric measurement word problems

practice.q: A bridge is 1 km 250 m long. Kim walks across it and back. How many meters does she walk?
practice.h: Change the length to meters. Across and back is 2 times the length.

practice.q: A pitcher holds 2 liters of water. Mr. Ali pours 4 glasses of 350 milliliters each. How many milliliters are left in the pitcher?
practice.h: Find how much he poured in all, then subtract from 2,000 mL.

practice.q: A puppy had a mass of 3 kg 400 g. A month later it had a mass of 5 kg 150 g. How many grams did it gain?
practice.h: Convert both masses to grams, then subtract.

practice.q: Which tape diagram matches "A red rope is 3 times as long as a 140 cm blue rope"?
ch: 3 equal bars of 140 cm for red and 1 bar of 140 cm for blue
1 bar of 140 cm for red and 3 bars of 140 cm for blue
1 bar of 420 cm for blue and 1 bar of 140 cm for red
3 bars of 140 cm for blue and 1 bar of 420 cm for red
practice.h: The red rope is made of 3 parts, each the size of the blue rope.

practice.q: A runner ran 2 km 600 m on Monday. On Tuesday she ran 1 km 900 m more than on Monday. How many meters did she run on the two days?
practice.h: First find Tuesday's distance, then add both days.

practice.q: Write a word problem using liters and milliliters that can be solved with 3,000 - 1,250. Solve it.
practice.ans: A jug has 3 liters of water and Ana drinks 1 L 250 mL. How much water is left? 3,000 mL - 1,250 mL = 1,750 mL, which is 1 L 750 mL.

quiz.q: A cat has a mass of 4 kg 200 g. A dog is 3 times as heavy as the cat. What is the dog's mass in grams?
A fish tank holds 30 liters. It has 18 L 750 mL of water in it. Kenji adds 5 buckets of 1 L 500 mL each. How many more milliliters are needed to fill the tank?
Pine Trail is 4 km 350 m long and Lake Trail is 3,980 m long. Which statement is true?
A roll of tape is 15 meters long. Ms. Ito uses 8 pieces that are each 75 centimeters long. How many centimeters of tape are left?
Three packages have masses of 1 kg 800 g, 2 kg 450 g and 950 g. What is their total mass in grams?
One batch of soup uses 750 mL of broth. Which is the smallest carton that has enough broth for 4 batches?
A board is 2 m long and a 35 cm piece is cut off. Jin says 1 m 65 cm is left. Lily says 165 cm is left. Who is right? Explain.
quiz.ans: Both are right. 2 m = 200 cm and 200 - 35 = 165 cm, which is the same length as 1 m 65 cm.

test.q: How many centimeters are in 9 meters?
How many grams are in 4 kilograms?
Which unit is best for measuring the distance between two cities?
How many milliliters are in 2 liters 75 milliliters?
Which is equal to 6,040 m?
Which mass is the least?
A water bottle holds 750 mL. How many milliliters do 4 bottles hold?
A board is 3 m long. A piece 1 m 45 cm long is cut off. How many centimeters of the board are left?
A melon has a mass of 1 kg 350 g and a pineapple has a mass of 2 kg 100 g. How many grams heavier is the pineapple?
A path is 2 km 80 m long. How many meters long is it?
Jada swims 750 m each day for 6 days. Her goal is 5 km. How many more meters must she swim to reach her goal?
A cook has 5 kg of rice. She uses 1 kg 250 g on Monday and twice that amount on Tuesday. How many grams of rice are left?
A school buys 8 bottles of paint with 450 mL in each bottle. Students use 2 L 900 mL of paint. How many milliliters of paint are left?
Which pair of lengths adds to exactly 1 km?
A conversion table shows 1 kg = 1,000 g, 2 kg = 2,000 g and 3 kg = 3,000 g. Which rule changes kilograms to grams?
Which statement is true?
Explain why 3 L 50 mL is not the same as 3,500 mL.
test.ans: 3 L = 3,000 mL, so 3 L 50 mL = 3,050 mL. 3,500 mL would be 3 L 500 mL.

test.q: Rico subtracted 6 kg 200 g - 2 kg 700 g and got 4 kg 500 g. Explain his mistake and find the correct answer.
test.ans: He subtracted 200 from 700 instead of renaming. Rename 1 kg as 1,000 g: 5 kg 1,200 g - 2 kg 700 g = 3 kg 500 g.

test.q: Describe how kilometers, meters and centimeters are related, and use the relationship to find how many centimeters are in 1 km.

Room 9 is planning a field day relay. (a) Each of 6 runners runs 450 m. How far do they run in all? Write the answer in meters and in kilometers and meters. (b) Each runner will drink 350 mL of water, and the coach has a 2-liter jug. Is there enough water? Tell how much extra or how much short. (c) An empty equipment bag has a mass of 3 kg 600 g. Four balls with a mass of 450 g each are put in the bag. What is the total mass? Show your conversions and explain each step.
rub: (a) 2,700 m = 2 km 700 m; (b) 2,100 mL is needed, so the 2 L (2,000 mL) jug is 100 mL short; (c) 3,600 + 1,800 = 5,400 g = 5 kg 400 g; conversions shown and each step explained.
All parts correct with gaps in explanation, or one small error with clear work.
One or two parts correct, or conversion errors throughout.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 3: Multi-digit multiplication and division
units.el: Draw area models on grid paper and label each partial product. Pre-teach "times as many", "factor", "multiple", "prime", "composite", "remainder" and "partial product", and contrast "3 times as many" with "3 more than" using cubes.

lessons.name: Multiplicative comparison and multiplying by 10, 100 and 1,000

practice.q: Which equation means "28 is 4 times as many as 7"?
practice.h: "Times as many" means multiply.

practice.q: A tree is 9 feet tall. A building is 5 times as tall as the tree. How many feet tall is the building?
practice.h: Draw a tape diagram with 5 bars, each the height of the tree.
Think 3 hundreds x 4.
How many thousands is 6 x 1 thousand?
Think 5 tens x 7 tens = 35 hundreds.

practice.q: Use the number 8 to explain the difference between "3 times as many" and "3 more than".
practice.ans: 3 times as many as 8 is 3 x 8 = 24. 3 more than 8 is 8 + 3 = 11. "Times as many" means multiply; "more than" means add.

quiz.q: Lily has 6 shells. Omar has 8 times as many shells as Lily. Which equation finds s, the number of shells Omar has?
A bike costs $120. A scooter costs 3 times as much as the bike. How many dollars does the scooter cost?
A sunflower is 4 times as tall as a tulip. The tulip is 25 cm tall. How many centimeters taller is the sunflower than the tulip?
Which is equal to 8 x 600?
Mina says 30 x 50 = 150. Explain her mistake.
quiz.ans: 30 x 50 = 3 tens x 5 tens = 15 hundreds, which is 1,500. She forgot that tens times tens make hundreds.

lessons.name: Multiplying up to four digits by one digit

practice.h: Multiply the ones, tens and hundreds, then add the partial products.
Use an area model with parts 1,000, 500, 20 and 6.

practice.q: Which shows the partial products for 6 x 347?
practice.h: Multiply 6 by each part: 300, 40 and 7.

practice.q: A theater has 7 sections with 245 seats in each section. How many seats are there?
practice.h: Multiply 7 by each place of 245.

practice.q: A school buys 3 boxes of paper with 1,250 sheets in each box and uses 2,975 sheets. How many sheets are left?
practice.h: First find how many sheets are in 3 boxes.

practice.q: Describe an area model for 5 x 2,314 and use it to find the product.

quiz.q: A farm packs 9 crates with 1,125 apples in each crate. How many apples is that?
Which is the best estimate for 7 x 389?
A family drives 286 miles each day for 4 days, then 175 miles on the fifth day. How many miles do they drive in all?
An area model has the parts 4 x 3,000, 4 x 200 and 4 x 6. Which expression does it show?
Tom multiplied 6 x 253 and got 1,218. Find his mistake and give the correct product.
quiz.ans: 6 x 5 tens = 30 tens, plus 1 regrouped ten is 31 tens, so 3 hundreds were regrouped. Tom did not add those 3 hundreds to 6 x 2 hundreds = 12 hundreds. 12 + 3 = 15 hundreds, so 6 x 253 = 1,518.

lessons.name: Dividing multi-digit numbers with remainders

practice.h: Share the 8 tens first, then the 4 ones.
What is the greatest multiple of 5 that is not more than 47?
Divide the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.
There are not enough thousands to share. Start with 45 hundreds.

practice.q: 58 students ride in cars that hold 4 students each. How many cars are needed?
practice.h: Can the leftover students be left behind?

practice.q: Explain how to check that 175 / 8 = 21 R7 is correct.
practice.ans: Multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder: 21 x 8 = 168 and 168 + 7 = 175. Since that equals the dividend, the answer is correct.

quiz.q: 92 pencils are shared equally among 8 students. How many pencils are left over?
A bakery makes 250 rolls and packs them in bags of 6. How many bags can it fill completely?
Which division has a remainder of 3?
Emma divided 4,812 by 4 and got 123. Explain her mistake and give the correct quotient.
quiz.ans: 4 thousands / 4 = 1 thousand and 8 hundreds / 4 = 2 hundreds. The 1 ten cannot be shared among 4, so the tens digit is 0 and the ten is regrouped as 10 ones; 12 ones / 4 = 3. She left out the 0 in the tens place; the quotient is 1,203.

lessons.name: Factors, multiples, prime and composite numbers

practice.q: Which number is a factor of 18?
practice.h: A factor divides 18 with no remainder.

practice.q: What is the next multiple of 7 after 49?
practice.h: Multiples of 7 go up by 7.

practice.q: Which number is prime?
practice.h: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.

practice.q: How many factors does 24 have?
practice.h: List the factor pairs: 1 x 24, 2 x 12 and so on.

practice.q: Which list shows all the factors of 20?
practice.h: Find every pair of whole numbers that multiply to 20.

practice.q: Explain why 9 is composite even though it is odd.
practice.ans: A composite number has more than two factors. 9 has the factors 1, 3 and 9, so it is composite. Being odd does not make a number prime.

quiz.q: Which number is a multiple of 6?
What is the greatest factor of 36 that is less than 36?
Which number is composite?
Which number is a multiple of both 3 and 4?
Mr. Lee arranges 30 chairs in equal rows. He wants more than 1 row and more than 1 chair in each row. How many different numbers of rows could he use?
Which statement is true?
ch: Every multiple of 6 is also a multiple of 3
Every multiple of 3 is also a multiple of 6

quiz.q: How many prime numbers are between 20 and 30?
Hugo says 2 is not prime because it is even. Explain why he is wrong.
quiz.ans: 2 has exactly two factors, 1 and 2, so it is prime. It is the only even prime number.

lessons.name: Multiplying two-digit by two-digit numbers

practice.h: Break both numbers apart: (20 + 3) x (10 + 4).

practice.q: Which partial products find 36 x 24?
practice.h: Multiply each part of 36 by each part of 24.
Use an area model with four parts.

practice.q: A school orders 28 boxes with 36 crayons in each box. How many crayons is that?
practice.h: Find 28 x 36 using partial products.

practice.q: Which is the best estimate for 49 x 31?
practice.h: Round each factor to the nearest ten.

practice.q: Use place value to explain why 40 x 30 = 1,200.
practice.ans: 40 x 30 = 4 tens x 3 tens = 12 hundreds, and 12 hundreds is 1,200.

quiz.q: A bus holds 48 students. How many students can 15 buses hold?
Which is one of the four partial products for 34 x 27?
Maria saves $15 each week for 26 weeks. Then she spends $199 on a tablet. How many dollars does she have left?
Which product is greatest?
Lin multiplied 26 x 13 like this: 20 x 10 = 200 and 6 x 3 = 18, so 26 x 13 = 218. Explain her mistake and find the product.
quiz.ans: She only multiplied tens by tens and ones by ones. She also needs 20 x 3 = 60 and 6 x 10 = 60. 200 + 60 + 60 + 18 = 338.

test.q: Which of these numbers is prime?
Ava has 9 cards. Sam has 5 times as many cards as Ava. Which equation finds s, the number of cards Sam has?
Which shows all the factor pairs of 16?
Which is the best estimate for 4,182 / 6?
Which expression shows 47 x 23 with partial products?
A theater sells 1,236 tickets for each of 4 shows. How many tickets does it sell in all?
A printer prints 2,345 pages and puts them in stacks of 5 pages. How many stacks does it make?
A farmer plants 34 rows with 18 trees in each row. How many trees does she plant?
437 students go on a field trip in vans that hold 9 students each. How many vans are needed?
A store orders 24 boxes with 36 markers in each box. It sells 650 markers. How many markers are left?
Leo's dog weighs 3 times as much as his cat. Together they weigh 48 pounds. How many pounds does the dog weigh?
A baker has 1,000 cookies. She packs them in boxes of 8 and sells each box for $6. How many dollars does she earn if she sells every box?
Mr. Patel has 75 photos. Each album page holds 6 photos. Which statement is true?
ch: He fills 12 pages and has 3 photos left for a 13th page
He fills 13 pages with none left over
He fills 12 pages and has 6 photos left

test.q: Which number is a multiple of 8 and also a factor of 64?
Describe how an area model shows 4 x 1,325 and find the product.
test.ans: Split 1,325 into 1,000, 300, 20 and 5. Multiply each part by 4: 4,000 + 1,200 + 80 + 20 = 5,300.

test.q: Ana says 51 is prime because it is odd and does not end in 5. Explain her mistake.
test.ans: 51 = 3 x 17, so its factors are 1, 3, 17 and 51. It has more than two factors, so it is composite.

test.q: 53 students need rides in cars that hold 4 students each. Ty says they need 13 cars because 53 / 4 = 13 R1. Explain whether he is right.
test.ans: He is not right. 13 cars hold only 52 students, so 1 student would have no ride. The remainder means one more car is needed, so they need 14 cars.

test.q: The garden club plants 16 rows of tulip bulbs with 24 bulbs in each row. (a) How many bulbs does the club need? (b) Bulbs are sold in bags of 9. How many bags must the club buy, and how many bulbs will be extra? (c) Each bag costs $7. What is the total cost? (d) The club has $300. Is that enough? Explain. Show your work with area models or partial products and explain what the remainder means.
rub: (a) 384 bulbs; (b) 384 / 9 = 42 R6, so 43 bags with 3 extra bulbs; (c) 43 x $7 = $301; (d) not enough, $1 short; correct work and a clear explanation of the remainder.
All parts correct with a weak explanation, or one small error with clear work.
One or two parts correct, or the remainder is ignored (42 bags).
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 4: Angle measure and plane figures
units.el: Act out quarter, half and full turns with arms and bodies. Keep a word wall with drawings for "ray", "vertex", "acute", "obtuse", "parallel", "perpendicular" and "line of symmetry", and let students use a paper square corner to test right angles.

lessons.name: Points, lines, rays and angles

practice.q: Which figure goes on forever in one direction only?
practice.h: Which figure has exactly one endpoint?

practice.q: What is an angle that measures less than 90 degrees called?
practice.h: Compare the angle with the corner of a sheet of paper.

practice.q: Two lines cross and form 4 right angles. What are the lines called?
practice.h: What is special about lines that meet at right angles?

practice.q: Two perpendicular lines cross. How many right angles do they form?
practice.h: Picture a plus sign.

practice.q: Which pair of streets is parallel?
ch: two streets that run side by side and never meet
two streets that cross at a corner
two streets that meet in a T
two streets that cross at a slant
practice.h: Parallel lines always stay the same distance apart.

practice.q: Explain the difference between a line segment and a ray.
practice.ans: A line segment has two endpoints, so it has a set length. A ray has one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction.

quiz.q: How many endpoints does a line segment have?
Which angle is obtuse?
ch: an angle wider than a square corner but less than a straight line
an angle that is exactly a square corner
an angle smaller than a square corner
an angle that forms a straight line

quiz.q: The capital letter T is made of two segments. How are the segments related?
Which capital letter has a pair of parallel segments?
How many pairs of parallel sides does a square have?
Which statement is always true?
ch: Perpendicular lines meet at right angles
Parallel lines meet at one point

quiz.q: How many acute angles does a right triangle have?
Dev says two lines that do not cross on his paper must be parallel. Explain why he might be wrong.
quiz.ans: Lines go on forever. Two lines that do not cross on the paper could still meet if they were extended. Only lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet are parallel.

lessons.name: Measuring angles in degrees

practice.q: How many degrees are in a full turn?
practice.h: A full turn goes all the way around a circle.

practice.q: How many degrees are in a straight angle?
practice.h: A straight angle is a half turn.

practice.q: An angle turns through 1/4 of a full circle. How many degrees does it measure?
practice.h: Divide the 360 degrees of a full turn into 4 equal parts.

practice.q: One ray of an angle passes through 0 on a protractor's outer scale, and the other ray passes through 125 on the outer scale. What is the angle?
practice.h: Read the same scale that has 0 on the first ray.

practice.q: Which is the best estimate for an angle that is a little smaller than a right angle?
practice.h: A right angle is 90 degrees.

practice.q: Explain how to use a protractor to measure an angle.
practice.ans: Place the center mark of the protractor on the vertex. Line up one ray with 0 on a scale. Read the number on that same scale where the other ray passes.

quiz.q: How many degrees are in a right angle?
A door opens 1/3 of a full turn. How many degrees does it turn?
One ray of an angle is at 0 on a protractor's inner scale. The other ray is at 70 on the inner scale and 110 on the outer scale. What is the angle?
Which angle measure is obtuse?
How many 1-degree turns make a half turn?
Sara turns 90 degrees and then 90 degrees more in the same direction. How much has she turned in all?
Ming measured an angle that looks smaller than a right angle and wrote 140 degrees. Explain his mistake and give the likely correct measure.
quiz.ans: He read the wrong scale on the protractor. An angle smaller than a right angle must measure less than 90 degrees, so it measures 180 - 140 = 40 degrees.

lessons.name: Adding angle measures and finding unknown angles

practice.q: An angle is split into two parts that measure 35 degrees and 50 degrees. How many degrees is the whole angle?
practice.h: When the parts do not overlap, their measures add to the whole.

practice.q: A right angle is split into two angles. One is 28 degrees. How many degrees is the other angle?
practice.h: The two parts add to 90 degrees.

practice.q: Two angles together form a straight angle. One measures 115 degrees. How many degrees is the other?
practice.h: A straight angle measures 180 degrees.

practice.q: Angles of x degrees and 47 degrees make a right angle. Which equation finds x?
practice.h: The two parts together make a right angle.

practice.q: Three angles meet at a point and fill a full turn. Two of them measure 120 degrees and 150 degrees. How many degrees is the third angle?
practice.h: Angles that fill a full turn add to 360 degrees.

practice.q: A ray splits a straight angle into two angles. Explain why the two angles add to 180 degrees.
practice.ans: Together the two angles make the straight angle, and they do not overlap, so their measures add to the measure of the straight angle, which is 180 degrees.

quiz.q: Angles of 64 degrees and 26 degrees are joined without overlapping. How many degrees is the total angle?
A straight angle is split into angles of 72 degrees and x degrees. What is x?
A round pizza is cut through the center into 6 equal slices. How many degrees is the angle of each slice at the center?
A right angle is split into three equal angles. How many degrees is each angle?
Four angles fill a full turn around a point. They measure 95 degrees, 85 degrees, 100 degrees and x degrees. What is x?
Two angles make a straight angle. One angle is 30 degrees greater than the other. What are the two angles?
A 35-degree angle and an unknown angle make a right angle. Jose says the unknown angle is 125 degrees because 90 + 35 = 125. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: The two angles together make 90 degrees, so he should subtract: 90 - 35 = 55 degrees. Adding gives a number larger than the whole angle.

lessons.name: Classifying two-dimensional figures and lines of symmetry

practice.q: A triangle has one angle that measures exactly 90 degrees. What kind of triangle is it?
practice.h: Which kind of triangle is named for a 90-degree angle?

practice.q: A triangle has three sides that are each 5 cm long. Which name fits?
practice.h: "Equi" means equal.

practice.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
practice.h: Count every fold that makes the two halves match, including the diagonals.

practice.q: Which quadrilateral always has two pairs of parallel sides and four right angles?
practice.h: Which shape must have square corners?

practice.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
practice.h: Try folding across the middle each way, then try the diagonals.

practice.q: Which triangle has no sides of equal length?
practice.h: Isosceles triangles have at least two equal sides.

practice.q: Explain how you can test whether a line is a line of symmetry.
practice.ans: Fold the figure along the line. If the two halves match exactly, the line is a line of symmetry.

quiz.q: A triangle has angles of 30, 60 and 90 degrees. What kind of triangle is it?
A triangle has angles of 110, 40 and 30 degrees. Which name fits?
How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
Which capital letter has exactly one line of symmetry?
Which statement is true?
ch: A square is a rhombus with four right angles
Every rhombus has four right angles
Every trapezoid has four lines of symmetry
Every triangle has a right angle

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
Mae says a triangle cannot be both right and isosceles. Explain whether she is right.
quiz.ans: She is not right. A triangle can have one 90-degree angle and two equal sides, like the triangle you get by cutting a square along a diagonal. It is a right isosceles triangle.

test.q: What is the measure of a right angle?
A figure has exactly one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. What is it?
How many degrees are in a half turn?
Which angle measure is acute?
Which lines never meet?
ch: lines that form a right angle

test.q: A right angle is split into angles of 38 degrees and x degrees. What is x?
Two angles form a straight angle. One measures 64 degrees. How many degrees is the other angle?
An angle measures 1/8 of a full turn. What is its measure?
A triangle has one angle greater than 90 degrees. What kind of triangle is it?
How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle 4 cm by 9 cm have?
Which shape has exactly 4 lines of symmetry?
ch: rectangle that is not a square

test.q: A fan blade turns 45 degrees each second. How many seconds does it take to make a full turn?
Four angles fill a full turn around a point. They measure 110 degrees, 75 degrees, 90 degrees and x degrees. What is x?
A desk lamp arm opens from 25 degrees to 140 degrees. How many degrees did it turn?
A straight angle is split into three angles of 40 degrees, 75 degrees and x degrees. What is x?
Which description fits a rhombus that is not a square?
