practice.q: Describe how to use an organized list to find the sample space for flipping a coin three times.
practice.ans: Choose H or T for the first flip, then each choice for the second and third flips: HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT. There are 8 outcomes.

quiz.q: A coin is flipped 3 times. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
Two number cubes are rolled. What is the probability that both show 6?
A spinner with equal red, blue and green sections is spun twice. What is P(red, then blue)?
A snack bar offers 4 drinks, 3 snacks and 2 sizes. How many combinations of one drink, one snack and one size are possible?
Two number cubes are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is greater than 9?
A bag has 1 red and 1 blue tile. A tile is drawn, put back, and a tile is drawn again. What is P(at least one red)?
A code is one letter from A, B, C or D followed by one digit from 0 to 9. A code is chosen at random. What is the probability that it starts with a vowel and ends with an even digit?
Pablo says that when two coins are flipped, the results are 2 heads, 2 tails or 1 of each, so P(1 of each) = 1/3. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: Those three results are not equally likely. The sample space is HH, HT, TH, TT, and one of each happens 2 ways out of 4, so P = 1/2.

lessons.name: Random sampling and comparing populations

practice.q: Which sample is most likely to represent all students at a school?
ch: 50 students chosen at random from the school roster
practice.h: A random sample gives every member of the population the same chance of being chosen.

practice.q: In a random sample of 60 students, 21 walk to school. The school has 900 students. About how many students walk to school?
Which survey question is biased?
ch: Don't you agree that our great park needs a new playground?
Do you think the park needs a new playground?
How often do you visit the park?
Which part of the park do you use most?

practice.q: Class A's quiz scores have a mean of 82 and Class B's have a mean of 76. Both have a MAD of 4. How many MADs apart are the means?
practice.h: Divide the difference of the means by the MAD.

practice.q: Why do different random samples from the same population give different results?
ch: Each sample includes different individuals by chance
Only one sample can be correct

practice.q: Explain why surveying people at a gym is not a good way to estimate how often people in a town exercise.
practice.ans: People at a gym probably exercise more than most people in town, so the sample is biased and does not represent the whole town.

quiz.q: A city wants to know how residents feel about a new bus route. Which method gives a random sample?
ch: Choose 200 names at random from a list of all residents
Ask 200 people at the bus station
Ask 200 people who call a radio show
Ask the first 200 people who answer an online ad

quiz.q: A random sample of 40 apples from an orchard has 3 bruised apples. The orchard has 6,000 apples. About how many are bruised?
Group A's mean time is 30 minutes and Group B's mean time is 24 minutes. Both groups have a MAD of 3 minutes. How many MADs apart are the means?
Two random samples of 50 seventh graders find that 18 and 22 students own a pet. What is the best estimate of the percent of all seventh graders who own a pet?
Plants given Fertilizer A have a median height of 24 cm and an IQR of 6 cm. Plants given Fertilizer B have a median height of 18 cm and an IQR of 6 cm. Which statement is supported?
ch: Plants with Fertilizer A tended to be taller
Every plant with Fertilizer A was taller than every plant with Fertilizer B
The plants with Fertilizer B were more varied
Both fertilizers gave the same results

quiz.q: In a random sample of 75 voters, 42 support building a new library and the rest oppose it. There are 12,000 voters. Based on the sample, about how many more voters support the library than oppose it?

Class A's reading times have a mean of 35 minutes and a MAD of 5 minutes. Class B's have a mean of 30 minutes and a MAD of 5 minutes. Is the difference between the classes meaningful? Explain using the MAD.
quiz.ans: The means differ by 5 minutes, which is only 1 MAD. The two sets of data overlap a lot, so the difference is not very meaningful.

test.q: A fair number cube is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number less than 3?
Which probability describes an event that is certain to happen?
A bag has 7 green beads and 13 orange beads. What is the probability of drawing a green bead?
A coin is flipped and a spinner with 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5 is spun. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
Three coins are flipped. What is the probability that all three land tails?
A basketball player made 34 of her last 40 free throws. What is the experimental probability that she makes a free throw, as a decimal?
Which is a random sample of a school's 800 students?
ch: 80 names drawn from a hat holding all 800 names
the 80 students in the library at lunch

test.q: A spinner is 1/3 red, 1/6 yellow and 1/2 green. In 300 spins, about how many times should it land on yellow?
Two number cubes are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 4?
P(A) = 0.3. Which statement is true?
In a random survey of 50 students, 18 prefer tacos for lunch. The school has 1,150 students. About how many students prefer tacos?
A game spinner has 8 equal sections: 3 are worth 10 points, 4 are worth 5 points and 1 is worth 0 points. What is the probability of scoring at least 5 points on one spin?
A quality check finds 4 broken pencils in a random sample of 250. A store orders 10,000 pencils. About how many will be broken?

A restaurant offers 3 appetizers (one is soup), 5 main dishes and 4 desserts (one is fruit). A meal of one of each is chosen at random. What is the probability that it includes the soup and the fruit dessert?
One random sample of 30 seventh graders sleeps a mean of 8.2 hours. Another random sample of 30 sleeps a mean of 7.9 hours. What is the best conclusion?
ch: Sample means vary, so the mean for all seventh graders is probably near 8 hours
One of the samples must be wrong
All seventh graders sleep exactly 8.05 hours

test.q: Team A's scores have a mean of 72 and a MAD of 6. Team B's scores have a mean of 90 and a MAD of 6. How many MADs apart are the means, and what does that suggest?
ch: 18 MADs; the teams score about the same
3 MADs; the teams score about the same
6 MADs; the difference is not meaningful

test.q: A spinner is spun 10 times and lands on green 6 times. Kai says the theoretical probability of green must be 3/5. Which response is best?
ch: 10 spins is too few; the theoretical probability depends on the sizes of the sections
The probability of green must be 1/2
The probability of green must be 6

test.q: On each of two days, the probability of rain is 2/5, and the days do not affect each other. What is the probability that it rains on both days?
Use a number cube to explain the difference between theoretical and experimental probability.
test.ans: Theoretical P(6) = 1/6 because there are 6 equally likely outcomes. Experimental probability comes from actual rolls; for example, 9 sixes in 40 rolls gives 9/40.

test.q: A school newspaper surveyed 40 students at a football game and found that 85% want more money for sports. The editor says 85% of all students want more money for sports. Explain the flaw and how to fix it.
test.ans: The sample is biased because students at a football game are more likely to support sports. The paper should survey a random sample from the list of all students before drawing a conclusion.

test.q: A class fair game uses two spinners. Spinner A has 3 equal sections (1, 2, 3) and Spinner B has 4 equal sections (1, 2, 3, 4). Both are spun and the numbers are added. A player wins if the sum is 6 or more. (a) Make a table or tree diagram of the sample space. (b) Find the probability of winning. (c) Predict how many wins there will be in 240 plays. (d) The class wants a fair game where P(win) = 1/2. Suggest a new rule using the sum and show that it is fair.
rub: (a) 12 equally likely outcomes listed; (b) sums of 6 or more: (2, 4), (3, 3), (3, 4), so P = 3/12 = 1/4; (c) 1/4 x 240 = 60 wins; (d) for example, win with a sum of 5 or more: 6 of 12 outcomes, P = 1/2; all work shown.
Sample space and probability correct with an error in the prediction or the new rule.
Sample space mostly correct but probability wrong.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 6: Geometry
units.el: Provide protractors, straws or strips for building triangles, and clay or foam solids to slice; label diagrams with supplementary, complementary, vertical, adjacent, cross section, base and height.

lessons.name: Unknown angle problems

practice.q: Two angles are supplementary. One measures 65 degrees. What is the measure of the other angle, in degrees?
practice.h: Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees.

practice.q: Two angles are complementary. One measures 38 degrees. What is the other angle, in degrees?
Two vertical angles measure (3x + 10) degrees and 70 degrees. What is x?
practice.h: Vertical angles are equal.

practice.q: Angles A and B together form a straight line, and angle A is 4 times angle B. What is the measure of angle B?
Three adjacent angles together form a straight line. They measure 47 degrees, x degrees and 85 degrees. What is x?
Explain how to find the angle that is supplementary to a 72-degree angle, and why your method works.
practice.ans: Supplementary angles together form a straight angle, which is 180 degrees. So the angle is 180 - 72 = 108 degrees.

quiz.q: An angle's complement measures 27 degrees. What is the angle, in degrees?
Two adjacent angles form a right angle. One is 2x degrees and the other is 3x degrees. What is x?
Four angles around a point measure 110, 95, x and 80 degrees. What is x?
Two lines cross, and one of the angles is 125 degrees. What are the other three angles?
Two supplementary angles measure (2x + 15) degrees and (x + 30) degrees. What is the measure of the larger angle, in degrees?
Which pair of angles is always equal?
Ana says two complementary angles can both be obtuse. Explain why this is not possible.
quiz.ans: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees. An obtuse angle is already more than 90 degrees by itself, so neither angle can be obtuse.

lessons.name: Constructing and drawing triangles

practice.q: Can 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm be the side lengths of a triangle?
ch: Yes, because 8 is the longest side
No, because all the lengths are different
practice.h: The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest side.

practice.q: Two angles of a triangle measure 50 and 60 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees?
practice.h: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees.

practice.q: Which set of side lengths can form a triangle?
Which conditions determine exactly one triangle?
ch: side lengths of 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm
side lengths of 2 cm, 3 cm and 5 cm

practice.q: A triangle's angles measure x, 2x and 3x degrees. What is the measure of the largest angle, in degrees?
Explain why knowing the three angles of a triangle does not determine a unique triangle.
practice.ans: Triangles with the same three angles can be different sizes, like scaled copies, so many different triangles have those angles.

quiz.q: A right triangle has an angle of 34 degrees. What is the other acute angle, in degrees?
Which set of lengths cannot form a triangle?
An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 40 degrees. What is the measure of each base angle, in degrees?
A triangle has sides of 4 cm and 9 cm. Which could be the length of the third side?
A triangle's angles measure (x + 10), (2x - 5) and (3x + 25) degrees. What is the measure of the largest angle, in degrees?
How many different triangles can be drawn with angles of 30, 60 and 90 degrees?
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2:3:4. What is the smallest angle, in degrees?
Explain whether a triangle can have two right angles.
quiz.ans: No. Two right angles already add to 180 degrees, which leaves 0 degrees for the third angle, so the sides could not meet to form a triangle.

lessons.name: Slicing three-dimensional figures

practice.q: A rectangular prism is sliced parallel to its base. What shape is the cross section?
practice.h: A slice parallel to the base has the same shape as the base.

practice.q: A cylinder is sliced perpendicular to its base, through the center of the base. What is the cross section?
A square pyramid is sliced parallel to its base. What is the cross section?
ch: a rectangle that is not a square

practice.q: A cone is sliced through its top point, perpendicular to its base. What is the cross section?
A rectangular prism is 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm. It is sliced parallel to its 8 cm by 5 cm base. What is the area of the cross section, in square cm?
Describe two different cross sections you can make by slicing a cube, and how to make each.
practice.ans: Slicing parallel to a face gives a square. Slicing off a corner, cutting the three edges that meet at that corner, gives a triangle.

quiz.q: A sphere is sliced by a flat plane. What shape is the cross section?
A triangular prism is sliced parallel to its triangular bases. What is the cross section?
A square pyramid is sliced perpendicular to its base, through its top point. What is the cross section?
A cylinder has a radius of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm. It is sliced parallel to its base. What is the area of the cross section, in square cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
A cylinder with a radius of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm is sliced perpendicular to its base, through the center of the base. What is the area of the cross section, in square cm?
Which cross section is NOT possible when a cube is sliced by one flat plane?
A loaf of bread shaped like a rectangular prism is 10 inches long, 4 inches wide and 4 inches tall. It is cut into slices 1/2 inch thick, parallel to its 4 in by 4 in end. How many slices are there?
Explain why a slice of a cone parallel to its base is a circle that is smaller than the base.
quiz.ans: Every slice parallel to the base has the shape of the base, a circle, but the cone narrows toward its top point, so slices closer to the top have smaller radii.

lessons.name: Area, surface area and volume problems

practice.q: A rectangular prism is 5 m by 4 m by 3 m. What is its volume in cubic meters?
A triangular prism has a triangular base with a base of 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. What is its volume in cubic cm?
practice.h: Volume = area of the base x length of the prism.

practice.q: A cube has edges of 2.5 inches. What is its surface area in square inches?
A figure is a 10 ft by 6 ft rectangle with a 4 ft by 2 ft rectangle cut out of it. What is its area in square feet?
A right prism's base is a trapezoid with an area of 18 square cm. The prism is 7 cm tall. What is its volume?
Explain why the volume formula V = Bh works for any right prism.
practice.ans: B is the area of the base. Stacking layers the same shape as the base, h units high, fills the prism, so the volume is the base area times the height.

quiz.q: A box is 12 in by 8 in by 5 in. What is its volume in cubic inches?
What is the surface area of a box that is 10 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm, in square cm?
A triangular prism's base is a right triangle with legs of 3 m and 4 m and a longest side of 5 m. The prism is 9 m long. What is its surface area in square meters?
A pool shaped like a rectangular prism is 20 ft long, 12 ft wide and 5 ft deep. It is filled to 80% of its depth. How many cubic feet of water are in it?
A cube-shaped box has a volume of 64 cubic inches. What is its surface area?

A storage shed is a rectangular prism 10 ft long, 8 ft wide and 7 ft tall, with a roof shaped like a triangular prism on top. The roof's triangle has a base of 8 ft and a height of 3 ft, and the roof runs the 10-ft length. What is the total volume of the shed in cubic feet?
Rafael says a 2 by 3 by 10 box holds more than a 4 by 4 by 5 box because 10 is the longest edge. Explain whether he is correct.
quiz.ans: He is not correct. Volume depends on all three edges: 2 x 3 x 10 = 60 cubic units and 4 x 4 x 5 = 80 cubic units, so the 4 by 4 by 5 box holds more.

test.q: Two angles are supplementary. One is 42 degrees. What is the other?
Two angles of a triangle measure 75 and 45 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees?
What is the cross section when a cylinder is sliced parallel to its base?
A box is 9 cm by 4 cm by 2 cm. What is its volume in cubic cm?
Vertical angles measure (5x - 12) degrees and (3x + 20) degrees. What is x?
Complementary angles measure x degrees and (2x + 15) degrees. What is the measure of the larger angle, in degrees?
Which set of lengths can form a triangle?
Which information determines exactly one triangle?
A right rectangular pyramid is sliced parallel to its base. What is the cross section?
A triangular prism has a base area of 15 square inches and a length of 8 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
What is the surface area of a cube with 6-meter edges, in square meters?
Four angles meet at a point and measure x, 2x, 3x and 4x degrees. What is the measure of the largest angle, in degrees?
A gift box is 12 in by 9 in by 4 in. Wrapping paper costs $0.02 per square inch. How many dollars does the paper to cover the box exactly cost?
A sandbox is 6 ft by 5 ft and is filled with sand 1.5 ft deep. Sand costs $3.50 per cubic foot. How many dollars does the sand cost?
A tent is a triangular prism. Its triangle end has a base of 6 ft and a height of 4 ft, and the tent is 9 ft long. What is the volume of the tent in cubic feet?
Angles A and B are supplementary, and angles B and C are supplementary. Which must be true?
A cube is sliced through the three corners that are each joined by an edge to one corner of the cube. What is the shape of the cross section?
ch: a rectangle that is not a square

test.q: In triangle ABC, angle A is 20 degrees more than angle B, and angle C is 40 degrees. What is the measure of angle A, in degrees?
An L-shaped garden is made of a 12 m by 5 m rectangle and an 8 m by 4 m rectangle that do not overlap. What is its area in square meters?
Explain how supplementary angles show that vertical angles are equal.
test.ans: When two lines cross, each of two vertical angles forms a straight line with the same angle between them. So each one equals 180 degrees minus that angle, which means the vertical angles are equal.

test.q: Bella says a triangular prism whose triangle has a base of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm, and whose length is 10 cm, has a volume of 400 cubic cm. Explain her mistake and find the correct volume.
test.ans: She multiplied 8 x 5 x 10 without taking half for the triangle. The base area is 1/2 x 8 x 5 = 20 square cm, so the volume is 20 x 10 = 200 cubic cm.

test.q: The school wants a planter shaped like a right prism. Each end is a trapezoid with parallel sides of 4 ft and 2 ft and a height of 1.5 ft, and the planter is 6 ft long. (a) Find the area of one trapezoid end. (b) Find the volume of soil that fills the planter. (c) Soil comes in 1.5-cubic-foot bags that cost $6 each. How many bags are needed, and what do they cost? (d) A second design is 25% longer with the same ends. By what percent does the volume increase, and why? Show your work.
rub: (a) (4 + 2) ÷ 2 x 1.5 = 4.5 square feet; (b) 4.5 x 6 = 27 cubic feet; (c) 27 ÷ 1.5 = 18 bags costing $108; (d) 7.5 ft long gives 33.75 cubic feet, a 25% increase, because volume is proportional to length when the base stays the same.
All parts set up correctly with one calculation error or a weak explanation in (d).
Base area or volume correct, but the bags or percent are wrong.
Little correct work.

math|8.about: Eighth grade works with integer exponents and scientific notation, uses rigid motions and dilations to understand congruence and similarity, solves linear equations and systems, defines and compares functions, models relationships with linear functions and scatter plots, finds volumes of cylinders, cones and spheres, and uses the Pythagorean theorem and irrational numbers.
std: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation and interpret scientific notation.
Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transformations and sequences of rigid motions and dilations.
Solve linear equations in one variable, including equations with rational coefficients and variables on both sides.
Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.
Construct a function to model a linear relationship and interpret its rate of change and initial value.
Apply the Pythagorean theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world problems.
Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres and use them to solve real-world problems.

units.name: Module 1: Integer exponents and scientific notation
units.el: Keep an exponent-rules chart with an expanded example for each rule (for example a^2 x a^3 = (a x a)(a x a x a)), and read numbers like 3.2 x 10^5 aloud as "three point two times ten to the fifth."

lessons.name: Exponent notation and products and quotients of powers

practice.q: Which expression equals 3^2 x 3^4?
practice.h: When you multiply powers with the same base, add the exponents.
Multiply -2 by itself 5 times. Is the product positive or negative?

practice.q: Which expression equals 7^9 ÷ 7^3?
practice.h: When you divide powers with the same base, subtract the exponents.

practice.q: Which number is equal to (-3)^4?
Explain why a^3 x a^4 = a^7 by writing out the factors.
practice.ans: a^3 x a^4 = (a times a times a) times (a times a times a times a). That is 7 factors of a in all, which is a^7.

quiz.q: Which expression equals 5^8 ÷ 5^2?
Which expression equals 4^3 x 4^5 ÷ 4^2?
Which expression is NOT equal to 2^10?
A colony of bacteria doubles every hour. It starts with 2^6 cells, so after 4 hours it has 2^6 x 2^4 cells. How many cells is that?
Jae says 3^4 x 3^2 = 9^6. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: When multiplying powers with the same base, keep the base and add the exponents: 3^4 x 3^2 = 3^6 = 729. He also multiplied the bases, and 9^6 is much larger than 729.

lessons.name: Power of a power, zero and negative exponents

practice.h: For a power of a power, multiply the exponents.
A negative exponent means a reciprocal: 5^-2 = 1 ÷ 5^2.

practice.q: Which expression equals (x^4)^3?
Which expression equals 2^-3 x 2^5?
Use a quotient of powers to explain why 4^0 = 1.
practice.ans: 4^3 ÷ 4^3 = 4^(3 - 3) = 4^0. Any nonzero number divided by itself is 1, so 4^0 = 1.

quiz.q: Which expression equals (2a^3)^2?
Which expression is equal to 1/8?
Which statement is true for every nonzero number x?
Mara says 6^-2 = -36. Explain her mistake and give the correct value.
quiz.ans: A negative exponent means a reciprocal, not a negative number. 6^-2 = 1/6^2 = 1/36.

lessons.name: Magnitude and scientific notation

practice.q: How is 0.00042 written in scientific notation?
practice.h: Move the decimal point so there is exactly one nonzero digit to its left.

practice.q: How is 3,600,000 written in scientific notation?
Write 7.05 x 10^4 in standard form.
Which number is greatest?
practice.h: Compare the powers of 10 first.

practice.q: Write 6 x 10^-3 in standard form.
Explain why 25 x 10^3 is not in scientific notation, and rewrite it correctly.
practice.ans: In scientific notation the first factor must be at least 1 and less than 10. 25 x 10^3 = 2.5 x 10^4.

quiz.q: Which number is written in scientific notation?
Write 9.1 x 10^-5 in standard form.
A human hair is about 0.00008 meter wide. How is this written in scientific notation?
About how many times larger is 6 x 10^9 than 2 x 10^6?
A city has about 4 x 10^6 people and a town has about 2 x 10^4 people. About how many times as many people live in the city as in the town?
Which list is in order from least to greatest?
There are 86,400 seconds in a day. When this number is written in scientific notation, what is the exponent on the 10?
Liam wrote 0.0052 as 5.2 x 10^3. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: 0.0052 is less than 1, so the exponent must be negative. Moving the decimal point 3 places to the right gives 5.2 x 10^-3.

lessons.name: Operations with scientific notation

practice.h: Multiply the first factors, then add the exponents.

practice.q: What is (5 x 10^4)(4 x 10^2), in scientific notation?
practice.h: 5 x 4 = 20. Rewrite 20 in scientific notation.

practice.q: (6 x 10^4) + (3 x 10^3) = ? Give the answer in standard form.
practice.h: Write both numbers with the same power of 10, or write both in standard form.

practice.q: Light travels about 3 x 10^5 km per second. About how far does it travel in 2 x 10^2 seconds?
Explain how to find (1.2 x 10^8) ÷ (4 x 10^3) and write the answer in scientific notation.
practice.ans: Divide 1.2 ÷ 4 = 0.3 and 10^8 ÷ 10^3 = 10^5, giving 0.3 x 10^5. Rewrite it as 3 x 10^4.

quiz.q: (7.5 x 10^5) - (5 x 10^4) = ? Give the answer in standard form.
The Sun is about 1.5 x 10^8 km from Earth, and light travels about 3 x 10^5 km per second. About how many seconds does sunlight take to reach Earth?
A computer does 4 x 10^9 calculations per second. How many calculations does it do in 1 minute?
A grain of sand has a mass of about 2 x 10^-6 kg. What is the mass in kilograms of 3 x 10^6 grains?
Nia says (4 x 10^3) + (2 x 10^3) = 6 x 10^6. Explain her mistake.
quiz.ans: She added the exponents as if multiplying. 4 thousand + 2 thousand = 6 thousand, so the sum is 6 x 10^3.

test.q: Which expression is equal to 2^4 x 2^3?
How is 0.0000607 written in scientific notation?
Which expression equals (5^2)^4 ÷ 5^6?
Which expression equals (3x^2)^3?
Write 4.3 x 10^6 in standard form.
(2 x 10^3)(4.5 x 10^2) = ? Give the answer in standard form.
Which number is the least?
Which equation is true?
A hard drive holds 2 x 10^12 bytes. A movie file is 4 x 10^9 bytes. How many movie files of that size fit on the drive?

About 3.3 x 10^8 people live in the United States, and about 3.9 x 10^7 live in California. Using these numbers, how many people in the United States do not live in California? Give the answer in standard form.

A blue whale has a mass of about 1.5 x 10^5 kg and a mouse has a mass of about 2 x 10^-2 kg. Using these numbers, how many times as massive as the mouse is the whale? Give the answer in standard form.
A cell is about 1 x 10^-5 meter wide. How many cells lined up end to end would stretch 3 x 10^-2 meter?
Which expression has the greatest value?
x is a positive number and x^5 x x^n = x^2. What is n?
Explain why 5^3 x 5^-3 = 1.
test.ans: Adding the exponents gives 5^(3 + (-3)) = 5^0 = 1. Also, 5^-3 = 1/5^3 = 1/125, and 125 x 1/125 = 1.

test.q: Priya says 4.5 x 10^-3 is greater than 1.2 x 10^-2 because 4.5 > 1.2. Explain her mistake.
test.ans: She must compare the powers of 10 first. 4.5 x 10^-3 = 0.0045 and 1.2 x 10^-2 = 0.012, so 1.2 x 10^-2 is greater.

test.q: The Moon is about 3.84 x 10^5 km from Earth and the Sun is about 1.5 x 10^8 km from Earth. A spacecraft travels at 4 x 10^4 km per hour. (a) How many hours would it take to reach the Moon? (b) How many hours would it take to travel the distance to the Sun? Write the answer in scientific notation. (c) Convert your answer to part (b) to days. (d) About how many times farther from Earth is the Sun than the Moon? Explain which exponent rules you used.
rub: (a) 3.84 x 10^5 ÷ 4 x 10^4 = 0.96 x 10^1 = 9.6 hours; (b) 1.5 x 10^8 ÷ 4 x 10^4 = 0.375 x 10^4 = 3.75 x 10^3 hours; (c) 3,750 ÷ 24 = 156.25 days; (d) about 400 times (about 390), with quotient of powers explained.
Three parts correct with clear work, or all parts set up correctly with one exponent error.
Correct setup for some parts but several errors in the powers of 10.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 2: The concept of congruence
units.el: Let students trace figures on transparencies or patty paper to act out each slide, flip and turn; post a chart of coordinate rules (reflect over x-axis: (x, -y); over y-axis: (-x, y); rotate 180: (-x, -y)) with pictures.

lessons.name: Translations, reflections and rotations

practice.q: The point (2, 5) is translated 4 units left and 3 units down. Where is its image?
practice.h: Moving left changes x; moving down changes y.

practice.q: The point (3, -2) is reflected across the x-axis. What is its image?
The point (4, 1) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise around the origin. What is its image?
practice.h: A 90-degree counterclockwise rotation around the origin sends (x, y) to (-y, x).

practice.q: A segment 7 cm long is reflected across a line. How long is the image, in cm?
Which feature of a figure might change after a rotation?
Explain why a rotation is called a rigid motion.
practice.ans: A rotation moves every point of a figure without stretching or shrinking it, so all lengths and angle measures stay the same.

quiz.q: Which transformation slides every point the same distance in the same direction?
The point (-5, 3) is reflected across the y-axis. What is its image?
The point (2, -6) is rotated 180 degrees around the origin. What is its image?
Triangle ABC has a 47-degree angle at A. After a reflection, what is the measure of the angle at A', in degrees?
A translation moves (1, 1) to (4, -1). Where does the same translation move (-2, 5)?
A rectangle with vertices (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 3) and (1, 3) is rotated 90 degrees around the origin. What is the area of the image, in square units?
P(3, 4) is reflected across the x-axis and then across the y-axis. Which single transformation gives the same image?
ch: a reflection across the line y = x

quiz.q: Kayla says the reflection of (2, 7) across the y-axis is (2, -7). Explain her mistake.
quiz.ans: Reflecting across the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate, so the image is (-2, 7). She reflected across the x-axis instead.

lessons.name: Sequences of rigid motions and congruence

practice.q: What does it mean for two figures to be congruent?
ch: One can be moved exactly onto the other by a sequence of rigid motions
They have the same shape but may be different sizes
They are in the same position

practice.q: The point (1, 2) is translated 3 units right and then reflected across the x-axis. What is the y-coordinate of the final image?
practice.h: Do the transformations in order, one at a time.

practice.q: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. AB = 9 and angle B = 40 degrees. Which must be true?
The point (-3, 4) is rotated 90 degrees clockwise around the origin. What is the x-coordinate of its image?
practice.h: A 90-degree clockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (y, -x).

practice.q: Which sequence maps (2, 3) to (-2, -3)?
ch: a reflection across the x-axis, then a reflection across the y-axis
a reflection across the x-axis only

practice.q: Describe a rigid motion that maps the triangle with vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 4) onto the triangle with vertices (-1, 1), (-3, 1) and (-1, 4).
practice.ans: Reflect across the y-axis. Each x-coordinate changes sign and each y-coordinate stays the same, which matches every vertex.

quiz.q: The point (4, -1) is translated 2 units up and then reflected across the y-axis. What is its final image?
Square ABCD has sides of length 6. It is rotated and then translated onto square EFGH. What is the perimeter of EFGH?
The point (3, 0) is translated 2 units right and then reflected across the y-axis. What happens if the order of the two moves is reversed?
Quadrilateral PQRS is congruent to quadrilateral WXYZ. Angle P = 85 degrees, angle Q = 95 degrees and angle R = 110 degrees. What is angle Z, in degrees?
Which two figures must be congruent?
ch: a figure and its image after a reflection followed by a rotation
a figure and its image after a dilation by a scale factor of 2
two rectangles with the same area
two triangles with the same three angles

quiz.q: The triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3) is reflected across the y-axis and then translated 5 units up. What is the area of the image, in square units?
Explain how you could show that two triangles on a coordinate grid are congruent.
quiz.ans: Find a sequence of translations, reflections and rotations that moves one triangle exactly onto the other. Rigid motions keep all lengths and angles, so the triangles are congruent.

lessons.name: Angle relationships with parallel lines and triangles

practice.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 65 degrees. What is the measure of its corresponding angle, in degrees?
practice.h: Corresponding angles are equal when the lines are parallel.

practice.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle measures 112 degrees. What is the measure of the same-side interior angle, in degrees?
practice.h: Same-side interior angles are supplementary when the lines are parallel.

practice.q: Two angles of a triangle measure 48 and 71 degrees. What is the measure of the exterior angle at the third vertex?
practice.h: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

practice.q: Alternate interior angles formed by parallel lines measure (3x + 5) and (5x - 25) degrees. What is x?
Which reason explains why the angles of every triangle add to 180 degrees?
ch: A line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side makes a straight angle from three angles equal to the triangle's angles
Every triangle has a right angle
The sides of a triangle add to 180

practice.q: Explain why alternate interior angles are equal when parallel lines are cut by a transversal.
practice.ans: One alternate interior angle is equal to its corresponding angle because the lines are parallel. That corresponding angle and the other alternate interior angle are vertical angles, which are equal. So the alternate interior angles are equal.

quiz.q: Two angles of a triangle measure 35 and 90 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees?
Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Same-side interior angles measure (2x + 20) and (3x + 10) degrees. What is x?
An exterior angle of a triangle measures 130 degrees. One remote interior angle measures 58 degrees. What is the other remote interior angle, in degrees?
Lines m and n are cut by a transversal, and two corresponding angles measure 70 and 75 degrees. What can you conclude?
ch: Lines m and n are not parallel
Lines m and n are parallel
The transversal is perpendicular to both lines
The lines are the same line

quiz.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and one of the angles is 90 degrees. What are the other seven angles?
ch: four are 90 degrees and four are 0 degrees
four are 90 degrees and four are 180 degrees

quiz.q: The angles of a triangle measure x, (x + 20) and (2x - 4) degrees. What is the measure of the largest angle, in degrees?
Tyler says that if a triangle has an exterior angle of 100 degrees, the interior angle next to it is also 100 degrees. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: An exterior angle and the interior angle next to it form a straight line, so they are supplementary. The interior angle is 180 - 100 = 80 degrees.

lessons.name: The Pythagorean theorem

practice.q: A right triangle has legs of 6 and 8. How long is the hypotenuse?
practice.h: Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

practice.q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 and one leg of 5. How long is the other leg?
practice.h: Subtract the square of the leg from the square of the hypotenuse.

practice.q: A 10-foot ladder leans against a wall with its base 6 feet from the wall. How many feet up the wall does it reach?
Which side lengths form a right triangle?
practice.h: Check whether the squares of the two shorter sides add to the square of the longest side.

practice.q: A rectangle is 9 cm by 12 cm. How long is its diagonal, in cm?
Explain how squares drawn on the sides of a right triangle with legs 3 and 4 show the Pythagorean theorem.
practice.ans: The squares on the legs have areas 9 and 16, which add to 25, the area of the square on the hypotenuse. So the hypotenuse is 5, and a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

quiz.q: A right triangle has legs of 7 and 24. How long is the hypotenuse?
A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 and a leg of 8. How long is the other leg?
Which set of side lengths could be the sides of a right triangle?
A TV screen is 32 inches wide and 24 inches tall. TVs are sized by the length of the screen's diagonal. What size is this TV, in inches?
A park is a rectangle 60 m by 80 m. How many meters shorter is the walk straight along the diagonal than the walk along two sides?
A right triangle has legs a and b and hypotenuse c. Which equation is true?
Zane says a right triangle with legs 5 and 12 has a hypotenuse of 17 because 5 + 12 = 17. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: The theorem adds the squares of the legs, not the lengths. 5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169, so the hypotenuse is the square root of 169, which is 13.

test.q: Which transformation is NOT a rigid motion?
ch: a dilation by a scale factor of 3

test.q: The point (-4, 2) is translated 5 units right. What is its image?
The point (6, -1) is reflected across the y-axis. What is its image?
The point (-2, 5) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise around the origin. What is its image?
Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 72 degrees. What is the measure of its alternate interior angle, in degrees?
Two angles of a triangle measure 38 and 64 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees?
An exterior angle of a triangle measures 145 degrees. One remote interior angle measures 80 degrees. What is the other remote interior angle, in degrees?
A right triangle has legs of 9 and 40. How long is the hypotenuse?
Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle XYZ. AC = 14 cm and angle C = 52 degrees. What is XZ, in cm?
Which transformation maps (5, 2) onto (-5, -2)?
Two lines are cut by a transversal, and a pair of corresponding angles both measure 58 degrees. What can you conclude?
ch: The lines meet at a 58-degree angle

test.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Same-side interior angles measure (4x + 8) and (2x + 10) degrees. What is the measure of the larger angle, in degrees?
A 25-foot ladder leans against a building with its base 7 feet from the building. How many feet up the building does the ladder reach?
A rectangular field is 45 yards by 60 yards. A player runs diagonally across it and back. How many yards does she run in all?
The angles of a triangle measure (x + 15), 2x and (3x - 15) degrees. What is the measure of the smallest angle, in degrees?
A figure is reflected across the x-axis and then translated 3 units up. Which statement about the final image is true?
ch: It is congruent to the original figure
It is larger than the original figure
Its angles are different from the original
It is similar but not congruent to the original

test.q: Which set of lengths forms a right triangle?
A square with vertices (1, 1), (4, 1), (4, 4) and (1, 4) is rotated 90 degrees around the origin. What is the perimeter of the image?
Use parallel lines to explain why the angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees.
test.ans: Draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. The two angles beside the triangle's angle at that vertex are alternate interior angles equal to the other two angles of the triangle. Together the three angles form a straight angle, 180 degrees.

test.q: Ruby says rotating (3, 1) 90 degrees counterclockwise around the origin gives (1, 3). Explain her mistake and give the correct image.
test.ans: She only swapped the coordinates, which is a reflection across the line y = x. A 90-degree counterclockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (-y, x), so the image is (-1, 3).

test.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 1), B(4, 1) and C(1, 5). (a) Find AB and AC, and use the Pythagorean theorem to find BC. (b) Reflect triangle ABC across the y-axis, then translate the image 2 units down. Give the coordinates of the final image A''B''C''. (c) Explain why A''B''C'' is congruent to ABC and give the length of B''C'' without measuring. (d) Find the perimeter and area of A''B''C''.
rub: (a) AB = 3, AC = 4, BC = 5; (b) A''(-1, -1), B''(-4, -1), C''(-1, 3); (c) reflections and translations are rigid motions that keep lengths, so B''C'' = 5; (d) perimeter 12 units and area 6 square units.
All parts correct with one error in coordinates or a weak explanation.
Lengths correct but transformations incorrect, or the reverse.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 3: Similarity
units.el: Give students grid paper and a center point to draw dilations by hand; post a chart that contrasts "same shape, same size" (congruent) with "same shape, scaled size" (similar), with matching pictures.

lessons.name: Dilations

practice.q: The point (2, 3) is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 4. What is its image?
practice.h: Multiply each coordinate by the scale factor.

practice.q: A segment 6 cm long is dilated by a scale factor of 1/3. How long is the image, in cm?
What does a dilation with a scale factor of 0.5 do to a figure?
ch: It shrinks the figure to half its size
practice.h: A scale factor less than 1 makes the image smaller.

practice.q: A triangle with a perimeter of 15 units is dilated by a scale factor of 2.4. What is the perimeter of the image, in units?
The point (-6, 9) is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 2/3. What is its image?
Explain how a dilation is different from a rigid motion.
practice.ans: A dilation multiplies every length by the scale factor, so the image can be larger or smaller, while angle measures stay the same. A rigid motion keeps both lengths and angles the same.

quiz.q: A figure is dilated with a scale factor of 3. Which statement is true?
ch: Every length is 3 times as long and the angles stay the same
Every angle is 3 times as large
The figure moves 3 units to the right
The area is 3 times as large

quiz.q: The point (5, -2) is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 3. What is the y-coordinate of the image?
A segment of length 12 has an image of length 9 after a dilation. What is the scale factor?
A 4 by 6 rectangle is dilated by a scale factor of 1.5. What are the dimensions of the image?
A 5 in by 7 in photo is dilated by a scale factor of 3. What is the area of the image, in square inches?
A point and its image after a dilation from the origin are (4, 10) and (6, 15). What is the scale factor?
A triangle is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 2, and then the image is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 1/2. How does the final image compare with the original triangle?
ch: It is exactly the same as the original
It is a reflection of the original

quiz.q: Ivan says dilating the point (3, 4) from the origin by a scale factor of 2 gives (5, 6). Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: He added 2 to each coordinate. A dilation from the origin multiplies each coordinate by the scale factor, so the image is (6, 8).

lessons.name: Similar figures

practice.q: What does it mean for two figures to be similar?
ch: One can be mapped onto the other by a sequence of rigid motions and dilations
They are exactly the same size

practice.q: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF, and the scale factor from ABC to DEF is 3. AB = 4. What is DE?
practice.h: Multiply the length by the scale factor.

practice.q: A 3 by 5 rectangle is similar to a larger rectangle whose longer side is 20. What is the shorter side of the larger rectangle?
practice.h: Find the scale factor using the longer sides.

practice.q: Are a 4 by 6 rectangle and a 6 by 8 rectangle similar?
ch: No, because 4/6 is not equal to 6/8
Yes, because each side increased by 2
No, because their perimeters are different

practice.q: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of 6 and 15. The smaller triangle's perimeter is 20. What is the perimeter of the larger triangle?
Explain why any two squares are similar.
practice.ans: Every square has four 90-degree angles, and one square can be dilated by the ratio of the side lengths and then moved to match the other square exactly.

quiz.q: Quadrilateral PQRS is similar to quadrilateral WXYZ. PQ = 8 and WX = 12. What is the scale factor from PQRS to WXYZ?
Triangle JKL is similar to triangle MNO. JK = 10, KL = 14 and MN = 15. What is NO?
Which rectangle is similar to a 6 by 10 rectangle?
Two similar figures have a scale factor of 2. How do their angles compare?
ch: The angles in the larger figure are doubled
The angles in the larger figure are halved

quiz.q: A 3 cm by 4 cm rectangle is dilated so that the image's longer side is 10 cm. What is the area of the image, in square cm?
Triangle A has vertices (0, 0), (2, 0) and (0, 1). Triangle B has vertices (0, 0), (-6, 0) and (0, 3). Which sequence maps triangle A onto triangle B?
ch: a dilation from the origin by 3, then a reflection across the y-axis
a dilation from the origin by 3 only

quiz.q: A model is similar to a real building with a scale of 1:200. The model is 45 cm tall. How many meters tall is the real building?
Kim says any two rectangles are similar because all their angles are 90 degrees. Explain her mistake.
quiz.ans: Similar figures need equal angles and proportional sides. A 2 by 3 rectangle and a 2 by 8 rectangle have equal angles, but 2/2 does not equal 3/8, so they are not similar.

lessons.name: Angle-angle similarity and indirect measurement

practice.q: Two triangles each have angles of 40 and 75 degrees. What can you conclude?
practice.h: If two pairs of angles match, the third pair must match too.

practice.q: A 6-foot person casts a 4-foot shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a 22-foot shadow. How tall is the tree, in feet?
practice.h: The person and the tree with their shadows form similar triangles.

practice.q: Triangle ABC has angles of 50 and 60 degrees. Triangle DEF is similar to triangle ABC. What is the largest angle of triangle DEF, in degrees?
Which pair of triangles must be similar?
ch: a triangle with angles 30, 60 and 90 degrees and another with angles 90, 30 and 60 degrees
two triangles that each have one 50-degree angle
two triangles with the same perimeter

practice.q: A 1.6 m tall student casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time, a flagpole casts a 15 m shadow. How tall is the flagpole, in meters?
Explain why two pairs of equal angles are enough to show two triangles are similar.
practice.ans: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees, so if two pairs are equal, the third pair is too. A dilation can then make one triangle the same size as the other, and rigid motions place it on top, so the triangles are similar.

quiz.q: A tree's shadow is 30 feet long. At the same time, a 5-foot post casts a 6-foot shadow. How tall is the tree, in feet?
Two right triangles are similar. The smaller one has legs of 3 and 4, and the shorter leg of the larger one is 12. How long is the longer leg of the larger triangle?
Triangle PQR has angles of 35 and 85 degrees. Which triangle must be similar to it?
ch: a triangle with angles of 60 and 85 degrees
a triangle with angles of 35 and 65 degrees
a triangle with angles of 35 and 90 degrees
a triangle with angles of 45 and 85 degrees

quiz.q: To find the width of a pond, Rosa sets up two similar triangles. The small triangle has sides of 8 m and 10 m. The matching sides of the large triangle are 36 m and x m, where x is the pond's width. What is x?
A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts the other two sides. Why is the small triangle that is formed similar to the large triangle?
ch: Corresponding angles are equal, so two pairs of angles match
All of their sides are equal

quiz.q: A mirror lies flat on the ground 12 m from a building. Lena stands 1.5 m from the mirror and sees the top of the building in it. Her eyes are 1.6 m above the ground. The triangles formed are similar. How tall is the building, in meters?
Owen says triangles with sides 3, 4, 5 and 6, 8, 12 are similar because two pairs of sides are doubled. Explain whether he is right.
quiz.ans: He is not right. Similar triangles need every pair of corresponding sides in the same ratio. 6/3 = 2 and 8/4 = 2, but 12/5 = 2.4, so the triangles are not similar.

lessons.name: Similar triangles and the Pythagorean theorem

practice.q: A right triangle has legs of 12 and 16. How long is the hypotenuse?
practice.h: Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

practice.q: Is a triangle with sides 10, 24 and 26 a right triangle?
ch: Yes, because 26 is the longest side
No, because all the sides are even

practice.q: A right triangle has legs of 5 and 12. A similar triangle has a hypotenuse of 39. How long is the shorter leg of the larger triangle?
practice.h: Find the hypotenuse of the first triangle, then the scale factor.

practice.q: A ramp rises 9 feet over a horizontal distance of 40 feet. How long is the ramp's surface, in feet?
Drawing the altitude to the hypotenuse of a right triangle makes two smaller triangles. How are they related to the original triangle?
ch: Both are similar to the original triangle
Both are congruent to the original triangle
Neither is similar to the original triangle
Only one is similar to the original triangle

practice.q: Explain how you know triangles with sides 6, 8, 10 and 9, 12, 15 are similar right triangles.
practice.ans: 6^2 + 8^2 = 100 = 10^2 and 9^2 + 12^2 = 225 = 15^2, so both are right triangles. Each side of the second is 1.5 times the matching side of the first, so they are similar.

quiz.q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 26 and a leg of 10. How long is the other leg?
A right triangle with legs of 8 and 15 is dilated by a scale factor of 3. How long is the hypotenuse of the image?
Which side lengths form a right triangle?

A kite string is 50 m long and pulled straight. The kite is directly above a point 30 m away from the person's hand, measured level with the hand. How high above the person's hand is the kite, in meters?
A 13-foot board leans against a wall, and its top touches the wall 12 feet above the floor. How far is the bottom of the board from the wall, in feet?
Both legs of a right triangle are doubled. What happens to the hypotenuse?
Use a triangle with sides 4, 5 and 6 to explain why a^2 + b^2 = c^2 works only for right triangles.
quiz.ans: For sides 4, 5 and 6, 4^2 + 5^2 = 41 but 6^2 = 36, so the equation is false. The relationship holds only when the angle between the two shorter sides is 90 degrees, and this triangle has no right angle.

test.q: The point (4, -2) is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 2.5. What is its image?
A 9-inch segment is dilated by a scale factor of 2/3. How long is the image, in inches?
Which transformation can map a figure onto a similar figure that is not congruent?
Which rectangle is similar to a 4 by 10 rectangle?
Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. AB = 7, BC = 9 and DE = 21. What is EF?
A segment of length 18 is dilated to a length of 6. What is the scale factor?
One triangle has angles of 45, 70 and 65 degrees. Another has angles of 70, 65 and 45 degrees. Which statement is true?
A 2-meter pole casts a 3-meter shadow. At the same time, a building casts a 27-meter shadow. How tall is the building, in meters?
A right triangle has legs of 15 and 20. How long is its hypotenuse?
Is a 3 by 5 rectangle similar to a 9 by 15 rectangle?
ch: Yes, with a scale factor of 3
No, because the sides grow by different amounts
Yes, with a scale factor of 6
No, because the areas are different

test.q: A map is a dilation of a park with a scale factor of 1/500. A path on the map is 14 cm long. How many meters long is the actual path?
A triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 6) is dilated from the origin by a scale factor of 1.5. What is the area of the image, in square units?

A lamppost and a 1.8 m tall student cast shadows that end at the same point. The student's shadow is 2 m long, and the student stands 4 m from the lamppost. The triangles formed are similar. How tall is the lamppost, in meters?
A right triangle has legs of 9 and 12. A similar triangle has a hypotenuse of 45. What is the perimeter of the larger triangle?
A figure is dilated from a point by a scale factor of 2, and the image is then dilated from the same point by a scale factor of 3. Which single dilation gives the same final image?
Which facts are enough to prove that triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF?
ch: angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E
angle C = 90 degrees and angle F = 90 degrees

test.q: The point (-8, 12) is dilated from the origin to (-2, 3). What is the scale factor?
A 6 by 8 rectangle is dilated by a scale factor of 1/2. How long is the diagonal of the image?
Explain how a dilation and rigid motions together can show that two triangles are similar.
test.ans: Dilate one triangle so its side lengths match the other triangle's side lengths, then translate, reflect or rotate it to place it exactly on the other. Because a sequence of these transformations maps one onto the other, the triangles are similar.

test.q: Ava says a 2 by 4 rectangle and a 4 by 6 rectangle are similar because each side grew by 2. Explain her mistake.
test.ans: Similarity needs the same scale factor for every side, not the same amount added. 4/2 = 2 but 6/4 = 1.5, so the rectangles are not similar.

test.q: Students measure a tree using shadows. At 3 p.m., a 1.5 m pole casts a 2 m shadow, and the tree casts a 16 m shadow on level ground. (a) Explain why the pole and its shadow and the tree and its shadow form similar triangles. (b) Find the height of the tree. (c) Find the distance from the top of the tree to the tip of its shadow. (d) The next morning, the tree's shadow is 9 m long. How long is the pole's shadow then? Show your work.
rub: (a) Both triangles have a right angle at the ground and the sun's rays make equal angles, so AA similarity applies; (b) 1.5/2 = h/16, h = 12 m; (c) 12^2 + 16^2 = 400, so 20 m; (d) 1.5/12 = s/9, s = 1.125 m; all reasoning explained.
Three parts correct with clear work, or all parts set up correctly with one calculation error.
Height correct but other parts missing or wrong.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 4: Linear equations
units.el: Model each solving step with a balance, and post the forms y = mx + b and ax + by = c with the words slope, rise, run, intercept and solution labeled on a graph.

lessons.name: Solving linear equations

practice.q: Solve 3(x - 2) = 2x + 4.
practice.h: Distribute, then collect the x terms on one side.

practice.q: Solve 0.5x + 3 = 2x - 9.

practice.h: Subtract 1/3 x from both sides first.

practice.q: Which equation has no solution?
How many solutions does 4(x + 2) = 4x + 8 have?
Explain how you can tell that 5x - 3 = 5x + 7 has no solution.
practice.ans: Subtracting 5x from both sides gives -3 = 7, which is never true, so no value of x makes the equation true.

quiz.q: Solve 7x - 5 = 3x + 19.
Which equation has exactly one solution?
Plan A charges $20 plus $15 per month. Plan B charges $50 plus $12 per month. After how many months do the plans cost the same total?
For which value of a does 2x + a = 2x + 5 have infinitely many solutions?
The sum of three consecutive integers is 87. What is the largest of the three integers?
Lea solved 6 - 2(x + 1) = 10 by first rewriting it as 4(x + 1) = 10. Explain her mistake and solve correctly.
quiz.ans: She subtracted 6 - 2 first, but multiplication comes before subtraction. Distribute: 6 - 2x - 2 = 10, so 4 - 2x = 10, -2x = 6 and x = -3.

lessons.name: Linear equations in two variables and their graphs

practice.q: Which ordered pair is a solution of y = 2x + 3?
practice.h: Substitute the x-value and check whether you get the y-value.

practice.q: The point (4, k) is on the line 3x + 2y = 18. What is k?
What does the graph of all the solutions of 2x + y = 6 look like?
Student tickets cost $5 and adult tickets cost $8, and ticket sales were $120, so 5s + 8a = 120. If 10 adults attended, how many students attended?
practice.h: Substitute 10 for a and solve for s.

practice.q: Which equation's graph passes through (0, 4) and (2, 0)?
Explain why the equation x + y = 10 has infinitely many solutions.
practice.ans: Any pair of numbers that adds to 10 is a solution, such as (3, 7), (4.5, 5.5) and (-2, 12). There are infinitely many such pairs, and together they form a line.

quiz.q: Which point is on the line y = -x + 5?
What is the y-intercept of the graph of 3x + 4y = 12?
What is the x-intercept of the graph of 3x + 4y = 12?
A line goes through (0, 0) and (5, 2). Which equation describes it?
Ty spends exactly $40 on pizza slices at $2.50 each and drinks at $1.25 each, so 2.5p + 1.25d = 40. If he buys 10 slices, how many drinks does he buy?
A line passes through (0, 3) and (1, 5). Which point is also on the line?
Mira walks at a steady rate, so d = 4t, where t is hours and d is miles. Explain what the point (3, 12) means on the graph, and what the 4 means.
quiz.ans: After 3 hours Mira has walked 12 miles. The 4 is her speed, 4 miles per hour, which is the slope of the graph.

lessons.name: Slope

practice.q: What is the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8)?
practice.h: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x.

practice.q: What is the slope of the line through (-2, 5) and (4, 2)?
What is the slope of a horizontal line?
A graph of a car's trip passes through (2, 110) and (5, 275), where x is hours and y is miles. What is the car's speed in miles per hour?
Which line is steepest?
practice.h: Compare the absolute values of the slopes.

practice.q: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope between any two points on a line is the same.
practice.ans: Slope triangles drawn between different pairs of points on the same line have the same angles, so they are similar. Their rises and runs are proportional, so rise ÷ run is the same everywhere on the line.

quiz.q: What is the slope of the line through (0, -3) and (4, 5)?
What is the slope of the line through (6, 1) and (-3, 7)?
A line goes down from left to right. What kind of slope does it have?
The line through (2, 4) and (x, 10) has a slope of 3. What is x?
Which two points lie on a line with a slope of 2?
A tank's water level was 120 cm after 2 minutes and 75 cm after 11 minutes, dropping at a constant rate. What is the rate of change of the water level, in cm per minute?
Ben says the slope of the line through (2, 3) and (5, 9) is 1/2 because (5 - 2) ÷ (9 - 3) = 1/2. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: He divided the change in x by the change in y. Slope is the change in y over the change in x: (9 - 3) ÷ (5 - 2) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

lessons.name: Equations of lines

practice.q: In y = -2x + 5, what is the y-intercept?
Which equation has a slope of 4 and a y-intercept of -3?
A line has a slope of 2 and passes through (3, 11). What is its y-intercept?
practice.h: Substitute into y = mx + b and solve for b.

practice.q: Which equation describes the line through (0, 6) and (3, 0)?
A line passes through (1, 4) and (3, 10). What is its y-intercept?
practice.h: Find the slope first.

practice.q: Explain why the graph of y = mx passes through the origin but the graph of y = mx + b does not when b is not 0.
practice.ans: For y = mx, x = 0 gives y = 0, so (0, 0) is on the line. For y = mx + b, x = 0 gives y = b, so the line crosses the y-axis at b instead of at 0.

quiz.q: What is the slope of y = 7 - 3x?
A line has a slope of -1/2 and passes through (4, 1). What is its y-intercept?
Which line is parallel to y = 5x - 2?
A line passes through (-2, 7) and (2, -1). What is its y-intercept?
A plumber charges a fixed fee plus an hourly rate. A 2-hour job costs $130 and a 5-hour job costs $250. What is the fixed fee, in dollars?
Which equation describes the same line as 2x + y = 8?
Write the equation of the line with a slope of 4 that passes through (0, -3), and explain what each part means.
quiz.ans: y = 4x - 3. The 4 means y increases by 4 each time x increases by 1, and -3 is where the line crosses the y-axis.

lessons.name: Systems of linear equations

practice.q: Which point solves both y = x + 2 and y = 2x?
practice.h: Check the point in both equations.

practice.q: What is the solution of the system x + y = 10 and x - y = 4?
Solve the system y = 3x and x + y = 12. What is y?
Two lines have the same slope and different y-intercepts. How many solutions does the system have?
Solve the system y = 2x - 1 and y = -x + 5. What is x?
practice.h: Set the two expressions for y equal to each other.

practice.q: Explain what the solution of a system of two linear equations means on a graph.
practice.ans: It is the point where the two lines cross. That ordered pair makes both equations true at the same time.

quiz.q: Solve the system 2x + y = 11 and y = x - 1. What is x?
Solve the system 3x + 2y = 16 and x - 2y = 0. What is y?
How many solutions does the system y = 2x + 1 and 2y = 4x + 2 have?
Adult tickets cost $8 and child tickets cost $5. Twenty tickets cost $130 in all. Which system models this?
Adult tickets cost $8 and child tickets cost $5. Exactly 20 tickets were sold for $130. How many adult tickets were sold?
A farm has chickens and goats. Together they have 30 heads and 74 legs. How many goats are there?
Explain how you can tell from the equations alone that y = 3x + 2 and y = 3x - 4 have no solution.
quiz.ans: The lines have the same slope, 3, but different y-intercepts, so they are parallel and never cross. No point is on both lines.

test.q: What is the slope of y = 6x - 1?
Solve 5x + 4 = 2x + 19.
Solve 3(x + 4) = 5x - 2.
How many solutions does 6x - 2 = 2(3x - 1) have?
Which of these equations has no solution?
What is the slope of the line through (-3, 4) and (5, -2)?
Which equation describes the line through (0, -2) with a slope of 3/4?
A line has a slope of -3 and passes through (2, 1). What is its y-intercept?
What is the solution of the system y = x + 4 and y = -2x + 1?
Solve the system x + 2y = 14 and x - y = 2. What is x?
Which system has infinitely many solutions?
One plumber charges $65 per visit plus $40 per hour. Another charges $95 per visit plus $30 per hour. For how many hours of work do they charge the same amount?
A school sold 300 tickets to a show. Student tickets cost $4 and adult tickets cost $7, and the school collected $1,560. How many student tickets were sold?
The perimeter of a rectangle is 46 cm. Its length is 5 cm more than twice its width. What is its length, in cm?
The cost of a taxi ride is a linear function of distance. A 4-mile ride costs $14 and a 10-mile ride costs $29. What is the starting fee, in dollars?
A jar holds 40 coins, all dimes and quarters, worth $6.25 in all. How many quarters are in the jar?
The lines y = ax + 3 and y = 2x + b form a system. For which values does the system have no solution?
A line goes down 3 units for every 2 units it goes to the right. What is its slope?
Explain how to tell, without graphing, whether a system of two linear equations has one solution, no solution or infinitely many solutions.
test.ans: Write both equations in y = mx + b form. Different slopes mean one solution. The same slope with different y-intercepts means no solution. The same slope and the same y-intercept mean infinitely many solutions.

test.q: Malik solved 2(x - 3) = 2x - 6 and wrote "x = 0, so the only solution is 0." Explain his mistake.
test.ans: Distributing gives 2x - 6 = 2x - 6, which is true for every value of x. The equation has infinitely many solutions, not only 0.

test.q: Gym A charges $30 to join plus $20 a month. Gym B has no joining fee and charges $35 a month. (a) Write an equation for the total cost y of each gym after x months. (b) Make a table or graph for 0 to 4 months. (c) Solve the system to find when the gyms cost the same, and give that cost. (d) Recommend a gym for someone who will stay 12 months, and justify your choice with costs.
rub: (a) y = 20x + 30 and y = 35x; (b) A: 30, 50, 70, 90, 110 and B: 0, 35, 70, 105, 140; (c) 2 months, $70; (d) Gym A ($270 compared with $420 for Gym B), with a clear justification.
Equations and comparison correct with one error in the table or a weak justification.
One equation correct and some correct values.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 5: Examples of functions from geometry
units.el: Use input-output "machine" diagrams for functions, and keep labeled models of a cylinder, a cone and a sphere with their formulas; pre-teach input, output, rule, radius, diameter and volume.

lessons.name: Functions and their representations

practice.q: Which relation is NOT a function?
practice.h: A function gives exactly one output for each input.

practice.q: A function's rule is y = 3x - 4. What is the output when the input is 6?
Which pairing is a function?
ch: input: a student's ID number; output: that student's name
input: an age in years; output: a person who is that age
input: a shoe size; output: the height of a person who wears that size
input: a letter of the alphabet; output: a word that starts with that letter

practice.q: A function's rule is "multiply the input by 4, then add 1." What input gives an output of 29?
practice.h: Work backward: subtract 1, then divide by 4.

practice.q: A vertical line crosses a graph at two points. What does this show?
ch: The graph is not a function
The graph is a linear function

practice.q: Explain why the table x: 2, 2, 5 and y: 3, 7, 9 does not represent a function.
practice.ans: The input 2 is paired with two outputs, 3 and 7. A function must assign exactly one output to each input.

quiz.q: A function's rule is y = 2x - 5. What is y when x = 8?
Which table represents a function?
A taxi ride costs C = 2m + 3 dollars for m miles. How many miles long was a ride that cost $21?
The distance a car travels at 60 miles per hour is a function of time. What is the input of this function?
A function's input is the side length s of a square and its output is the square's perimeter. What is the output when s = 7.5?
Which statement about functions is true?
ch: Two different inputs can have the same output
One input can have two different outputs
The graph of every function is a straight line
Every function has a negative output

quiz.q: A tank holds 500 liters of water and drains so that the amount left after t minutes is A = 500 - 25t liters. After how many minutes are 150 liters left?
Rosa says the points (3, 1), (3, 4) and (3, 9) form a function because every output is different. Explain her mistake.
quiz.ans: The input 3 is paired with three different outputs. For a function, each input must have exactly one output, so these points do not form a function.

lessons.name: Linear and nonlinear functions

practice.q: Which equation defines a nonlinear function?
practice.h: A linear function has a constant rate of change, and its graph is a straight line.

practice.q: Which table shows a linear function?
A linear function has the table x: 0, 1, 2 and y: 6, 10, 14. What is its rate of change?
Function A is y = 3x + 2. Function B has the table x: 0, 2, 4 and y: 1, 9, 17. How much greater is Function B's rate of change than Function A's?
practice.h: Find the rate of change of each function first.

practice.q: The area of a square is a function of its side length, A = s^2. Is this function linear?
ch: No, because the area does not change by a constant amount for each unit of side length
Yes, because the graph goes up
Yes, because it has one input
No, because squares have four sides

practice.q: Explain how you can tell from a table whether a function is linear.
practice.ans: When the inputs change by equal steps, a linear function's outputs also change by equal amounts. If the outputs change by different amounts for equal steps, the function is nonlinear.

quiz.q: Which graph represents a linear function?
ch: a straight line that is not vertical

quiz.q: Function B's graph is a straight line through (0, 5) and (3, 11). What is its rate of change?
Function A is y = 5x - 1. Function B has the table x: 1, 2, 3 and y: 6, 10, 14. Which statement is true?
ch: Function A has the greater rate of change
Function B has the greater rate of change
They have the same rate of change

quiz.q: The volume of a cube with edge length e is V = e^3. What is the volume when e = 4?
Which situation is modeled by a nonlinear function?
ch: the area of a circle as a function of its radius
the cost of apples at $2 per pound
the distance traveled at a steady 50 miles per hour
savings that grow by $10 each week

quiz.q: Car A travels d = 55t miles in t hours. Car B's distances are 48, 96 and 144 miles after 1, 2 and 3 hours, at a constant speed. After 4 hours, how many more miles has Car A traveled than Car B?
Which function has a constant rate of change of -3?
Kai says y = 2x^2 is linear because 2 is a constant rate of change. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: Because x is squared, the outputs for x = 0, 1, 2, 3 are 0, 2, 8 and 18. They increase by 2, 6 and 10, which is not a constant rate of change, so the function is nonlinear.

lessons.name: Volume of cylinders

practice.q: What is the volume of a cylinder with a radius of 2 cm and a height of 5 cm, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
practice.h: V = pi x r^2 x h.

practice.q: A cylindrical can has a diameter of 8 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
practice.h: Find the radius first.

practice.q: A cylinder has a base area of 28.26 square inches and a height of 12 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
A cylinder's height is doubled and its radius stays the same. What happens to its volume?
A cylindrical tank has a radius of 3 m and a volume of 141.3 cubic meters. What is its height in meters? Use 3.14 for pi.
Explain how the volume formula for a cylinder is like the volume formula for a prism.
practice.ans: Both are the area of the base times the height. A cylinder's base is a circle with area pi x r^2, so its volume is pi x r^2 x h.

quiz.q: What is the volume of a cylinder with a radius of 10 m and a height of 3 m, in cubic meters? Use 3.14 for pi.
A water bottle is a cylinder with a radius of 3.5 cm and a height of 20 cm. What is its volume in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
Which cylinder holds more?
A cylindrical wading pool has a diameter of 6 m and is filled to a depth of 1.5 m. Water costs $2 per cubic meter. How many dollars does the water cost? Use 3.14 for pi.
A cylinder's radius is doubled and its height stays the same. By what number is its volume multiplied?
A cylinder has a volume of 100.48 cubic inches and a height of 8 inches. What is its radius? Use 3.14 for pi.
A cylindrical candle has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm. Wax costs $0.05 per cubic cm. How many dollars does the wax cost? Use 3.14 for pi.
Jin found the volume of a cylinder with a diameter of 10 and a height of 4 as 3.14 x 10^2 x 4 = 1,256. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: He used the diameter instead of the radius. The radius is 5, so V = 3.14 x 25 x 4 = 314 cubic units.

lessons.name: Volume of cones and spheres

practice.q: What is the volume of a cone with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
practice.h: V = 1/3 x pi x r^2 x h.

practice.q: What is the volume of a sphere with a radius of 3 m, in cubic meters? Use 3.14 for pi.
practice.h: V = 4/3 x pi x r^3.

practice.q: A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and the same height. How do their volumes compare?
ch: The cone's volume is 1/3 of the cylinder's
The cone's volume is 1/2 of the cylinder's
The cone's volume is 3 times the cylinder's

practice.q: A cone has a diameter of 12 inches and a height of 5 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches? Use 3.14 for pi.
A ball has a radius of 6 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches? Use 3.14 for pi.
Explain how many full cones of water it takes to fill a cylinder with the same radius and height, and why.
practice.ans: Three. The cone's volume is 1/3 x pi x r^2 x h, which is one third of the cylinder's volume, pi x r^2 x h.

quiz.q: What is the volume of a cone with a radius of 2 ft and a height of 6 ft, in cubic feet? Use 3.14 for pi.
What is the volume of a sphere with a radius of 1.5 cm, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
Which expression gives the volume of a sphere with radius r?

An ice cream cone has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm and is filled level with ice cream. A half-sphere scoop with a radius of 3 cm sits on top. What is the total volume of ice cream, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
A cylinder holds 150.72 cubic inches. How many cubic inches does a cone with the same radius and height hold?
A cylinder, a cone and a sphere each have a radius of 3. The cylinder and the cone each have a height of 6. Which has the greatest volume?
A bowl is a half sphere with a radius of 9 cm. How many cubic cm of soup does it hold when full? Use 3.14 for pi.
Pat says a sphere with a radius of 3 has a volume of 4/3 x 3.14 x 3^2 = 37.68. Explain the mistake and find the correct volume.
quiz.ans: The radius must be cubed, not squared. V = 4/3 x 3.14 x 27 = 113.04 cubic units.

test.q: Which set of ordered pairs is a function?
A function's rule is y = 4x + 3. What is y when x = 5?
Which formula gives the volume of a cylinder?
ch: V = pi x r^2 x h
V = 1/3 x pi x r^2 x h
V = 2 x pi x r x h

test.q: Which equation defines a linear function?
Which table does NOT represent a function?
What is the volume of a cylinder with a radius of 5 cm and a height of 8 cm, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
What is the volume of a cone with a radius of 6 in and a height of 10 in, in cubic inches? Use 3.14 for pi.
What is the volume of a sphere with a radius of 9 cm, in cubic cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
Function A is y = 2x + 7. Function B has the table x: 0, 1, 2 and y: 3, 6, 9. Which statement is true?
ch: B has the greater rate of change, and A has the greater initial value
A has the greater rate of change and the greater initial value
B has the greater rate of change and the greater initial value
They have the same rate of change

test.q: A linear function has the table x: 2, 4, 6 and y: 11, 17, 23. What is its rate of change?
A cylindrical water tank has a diameter of 4 m and a height of 3 m. It is 75% full. How many cubic meters of water does it hold? Use 3.14 for pi.
A spherical balloon with a radius of 3 cm is inflated until its radius is 6 cm. How many cubic cm of volume did it gain? Use 3.14 for pi.
A cone-shaped cup has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 9 cm. How many full cups of water does it take to fill a cylinder with a radius of 4 cm and a height of 18 cm?
A gym charges a $40 fee plus $25 per month, so the cost is C = 25m + 40 dollars for m months. Lia has $240. What is the greatest number of months she can pay for?
A cylinder and a sphere have the same radius r, and the cylinder's height is 2r. How do their volumes compare?
ch: The sphere's volume is 2/3 of the cylinder's
The sphere's volume is 1/3 of the cylinder's
The sphere's volume is twice the cylinder's

test.q: The radius of a sphere is tripled. By what number is its volume multiplied?
Which of these situations is modeled by a nonlinear function?
ch: the volume of a cube as a function of its edge length
the cost of gas at $4.50 per gallon
the perimeter of a square as a function of its side length
the distance walked at a steady 3 miles per hour

test.q: A cylinder has a volume of 471 cubic cm and a radius of 5 cm. What is its height in cm? Use 3.14 for pi.
Use the perimeter and the area of a square to explain the difference between a linear function and a nonlinear function.
test.ans: The perimeter P = 4s goes up by 4 each time s goes up by 1, a constant rate, so it is linear. The area A = s^2 gives 1, 4, 9, 16, which go up by different amounts, so it is nonlinear.

test.q: Dana says a cone with a radius of 3 and a height of 6 has a volume of 169.56 cubic units. Explain her mistake and find the correct volume. Use 3.14 for pi.
test.ans: She used the cylinder formula and left out the 1/3. The correct volume is 1/3 x 3.14 x 9 x 6 = 56.52 cubic units.

test.q: A juice company is choosing a container. Design A is a cylinder with a radius of 4 cm and a height of 12 cm. Design B is a cone with a radius of 6 cm and a height of 12 cm. Design C is a sphere with a radius of 6 cm. Use 3.14 for pi. (a) Find the volume of each design. (b) Which design holds the most? (c) The company needs a container that holds at least 500 cubic cm. Which designs work? (d) The company wants Design A to hold the same amount as Design C without changing its radius. What height should Design A have? Show your work.
rub: (a) A: 602.88, B: 452.16, C: 904.32 cubic cm; (b) Design C; (c) Designs A and C; (d) 904.32 ÷ (3.14 x 16) = 18 cm; formulas and work shown.
Volumes correct with an error in (c) or (d), or one volume wrong with otherwise correct reasoning.
One or two volumes correct, or formulas correct with radius and diameter mixed up.
