units.name: Unit 6: Medieval Europe (7.6)
units.el: Use a feudal pyramid diagram and a manor map with labels (castle, church, fields, village, mill). Pre-teach vassal, fief, serf, manor, pope, excommunicate, crusade, plague and charter with images, and use the frame "Because of ___, Europe ___."

lessons.name: Geography and the early Middle Ages

practice.q: The period in Europe from about 500 to 1500 CE is called the
practice.h: It comes between ancient times and modern times.

practice.q: Which geographic feature helped trade in medieval Europe?
ch: many navigable rivers and seas close to most land
practice.h: Look at the rivers such as the Rhine and Danube on a map.

practice.q: After Rome fell, which group brought Christianity to many peoples in Northern Europe?
ch: missionaries, including monks sent by the pope
practice.h: Ireland and England were reached by these religious travelers.

practice.q: The Frankish king crowned emperor by the pope on Christmas Day in 800 CE was
practice.h: His name means "Charles the Great."

practice.q: Charlemagne was crowned emperor in 800 CE and died in 814 CE. How many years did he rule as emperor?
practice.h: Subtract 800 from 814.

practice.q: Explain why the pope crowning Charlemagne in 800 was important.
practice.ans: It joined the power of the Church with the power of a Christian king, showed the pope's authority to crown rulers and created the idea of a new Western empire after Rome.
practice.h: Think about Church power and royal power together.

quiz.q: Charlemagne encouraged learning by
ch: starting schools and having monks copy ancient books

quiz.q: Monasteries were important in the early Middle Ages because monks
ch: preserved books, ran schools, cared for the sick and farmed

quiz.q: The historian Einhard, who knew Charlemagne, wrote about 830 that the emperor tried to learn to write late in life but began too late. What does this show?
ch: Even powerful rulers then were often not educated, which shows why Charlemagne valued schools

quiz.q: After Charlemagne's death, his empire
ch: was divided among his grandsons and weakened
became part of the Byzantine Empire

quiz.q: Raids by Vikings, Magyars and Muslims in the 800s and 900s led people in Europe to
ch: depend on local lords for protection

quiz.q: The Western Roman Empire fell in 476. Charlemagne was crowned in 800. How many years apart were these events?
Why did the Church become the most important unifying force in Western Europe after Rome fell?
ch: It was the one large institution that remained, with leaders, beliefs and Latin learning shared across many kingdoms
It was ruled by the Byzantine emperor

quiz.q: Explain how monasteries helped preserve learning during the early Middle Ages.
quiz.ans: Monks copied ancient and religious books by hand, kept libraries and ran schools, so knowledge from Rome and the Bible survived when cities and schools declined.

lessons.name: Feudalism and the manor

practice.q: Feudalism was a system in which
ch: lords gave land to vassals in exchange for loyalty and military service
practice.h: Land was traded for service.

practice.q: A piece of land granted by a lord to a vassal was called a
practice.h: The word is related to "feudal."

practice.q: Serfs were
ch: peasants bound to the land who worked for the lord and could not leave without permission
practice.h: They were not enslaved, but they were not free either.

practice.q: A manor was
ch: a lord's estate with fields, a village, a mill and a church that produced most of what people needed
a city with walls and merchants
practice.h: Manors were nearly self-sufficient.

practice.q: A serf had to work 3 days a week in the lord's fields. How many days is that in 12 weeks?
practice.h: Multiply 3 by 12.

practice.q: Explain how feudalism provided protection in a time of invasions.
practice.ans: Kings could not defend every area, so they gave land to lords, who gave land to knights; knights defended the lord's land and peasants, and peasants farmed in exchange for protection.
practice.h: Who protected whom, and what did each group give?

quiz.q: Knights followed a code of behavior called
Which statement about serfs is accurate?
ch: They farmed the lord's land, paid him part of their crops and could not leave without permission
They were free to move anywhere

quiz.q: Why was the manor system mostly self-sufficient?
ch: Trade had declined, so manors produced their own food, cloth and tools
Manors traded with China every day
Kings sent food to every manor

quiz.q: A noble woman on a manor often
ch: managed the household and estate and could run it when her husband was away
served as a knight in battle

quiz.q: How did feudalism in Europe resemble feudalism in Japan?
ch: Warriors served lords in exchange for land or support

quiz.q: A manor had 600 acres of farmland. The lord kept 1/3 of it for himself. How many acres did the lord keep?
Which change would most weaken the manor system?
ch: The growth of towns and trade that gave serfs a chance to earn money elsewhere

quiz.q: Compare the life of a knight and the life of a serf on a manor.
quiz.ans: A knight was a noble warrior who received land and owed military service and loyalty to his lord. A serf was a peasant bound to the land who farmed, paid crops and labor to the lord and received protection but had little freedom.

lessons.name: Church and kings: power, law and the Magna Carta

practice.q: The leader of the Roman Catholic Church is the
practice.h: He lived in Rome.

practice.q: Excommunication meant
ch: being cut off from the Church and its sacraments
practice.h: Medieval people believed this could cost them their salvation.

practice.q: In 1077, Emperor Henry IV stood in the snow at Canossa to ask Pope Gregory VII for forgiveness. What does this show?
ch: The pope had great power, even over emperors
practice.h: Who had to ask whom for forgiveness?

practice.q: The Magna Carta, signed by King John of England in 1215,
ch: limited the power of the king and protected certain rights of nobles and free men
practice.h: Nobles forced the king to agree.

practice.q: The Magna Carta was signed in 1215. The U.S. Constitution was written in 1787. How many years apart were these documents?
practice.h: Subtract 1215 from 1787.

practice.q: The Magna Carta (1215, adapted translation) says that no free man shall be imprisoned or have his property taken "except by the lawful judgment of his peers or by the law of the land." Explain why this idea was important.
practice.ans: It meant even the king had to follow the law and could not punish people without a fair legal process, which became the basis for ideas such as trial by jury and due process.
practice.h: Who else besides ordinary people had to follow the law?

quiz.q: Medieval kings and popes struggled over
ch: who had the right to appoint bishops and who held more authority

quiz.q: Parliament in England, which grew in the 1200s,
ch: gave nobles and later townspeople a voice in approving taxes and laws
was a court for the pope

quiz.q: English common law developed from
ch: judges' decisions in earlier cases that became the basis for later rulings

quiz.q: Which right in the U.S. Constitution can be traced partly to the Magna Carta?
ch: due process of law and trial by jury

quiz.q: Why did the Church hold so much power in medieval life?
ch: It controlled sacraments, owned large lands, collected tithes and ran schools and charities

quiz.q: A peasant family harvested 400 bushels of grain and paid a tithe of 1/10 to the Church. How many bushels did they pay?
Why did English nobles force King John to accept the Magna Carta?
ch: He raised heavy taxes and punished nobles without fair trials
He gave them too much land

quiz.q: Source A: King John raised taxes heavily to pay for wars and seized nobles' lands without trials. Source B: In 1215, nobles forced John to agree to the Magna Carta, which said a free man could not be imprisoned or lose his property except by the lawful judgment of his peers or the law of the land. Source C: Centuries later, the U.S. Bill of Rights promised that no person shall be deprived of life, liberty or property without due process of law. Make a claim about the importance of the Magna Carta. Use evidence from the sources and explain your reasoning.
quiz.ans: Claim: The Magna Carta was important because it set the idea that rulers must follow the law, an idea that shaped later governments. Evidence: Source A shows John abused his power. Source B shows the Magna Carta required lawful judgment before punishment. Source C shows the U.S. Bill of Rights promises due process. Reasoning: The Magna Carta limited a king's power by law, and the same idea of protecting people from unfair punishment appears in the Bill of Rights, showing its lasting influence.
rub: Clear, accurate claim; relevant and sufficient evidence; reasoning that explains how the evidence supports the claim using key ideas from the unit.
Accurate claim and relevant evidence; the reasoning is only partly explained.
A claim with limited or partly relevant evidence and little reasoning.
The claim is unclear or inaccurate, with little or no evidence or reasoning.

lessons.name: The Crusades and the Reconquista

practice.q: The Crusades were a series of
ch: military expeditions by European Christians to win control of the Holy Land
practice.h: They began in 1096.

practice.q: In 1095, Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade to
ch: take control of Jerusalem and help the Byzantine Empire against the Seljuk Turks
practice.h: The Byzantine emperor had asked for help.

practice.q: Jerusalem is a holy city to

practice.h: These three crops are sometimes called the "three sisters."

practice.h: Many are carved on stone monuments.

practice.h: Multiply 3 by 20, then add 5.

practice.q: Explain why Maya priests and rulers valued their calendars so highly.
practice.ans: Calendars told them when to plant and harvest and when to hold religious ceremonies, and knowledge of the calendar gave priests and kings authority.
practice.h: Think about farming and religion.

quiz.q: Maya mathematicians used a symbol for zero, which shows that they

quiz.ans: Farmers cut and burned forest to clear fields, and some built raised fields and terraces; the thin soil wore out, so fields had to be moved or managed carefully.

practice.h: Subtract 1325 from 1519.

soc|8.about: Eighth graders study the United States from the Revolution to 1914: the ideas of the founding, the Constitution and Bill of Rights, the early republic, the growth of the North, South and West, slavery and the abolition movement, the Civil War, Reconstruction and the rise of industry and immigration. std: Students understand the major events preceding the founding of the nation and relate their significance to the development of American constitutional democracy.

practice.h: He had commanded the Continental Army.
